key: Opening a restaurant is not just
name: ch00_restaurant_four_roles
alt: A busy Indian restaurant cut away like a doll's house, showing four people doing four different jobs, while a lone home cook outside looks overwhelmed.
scene: A cut-away view of a small two-storey Indian restaurant at lunch rush, drawn like a doll's house with the front wall removed so four rooms are visible at once, read left to right. Far left, at the back door, a wiry man in his 40s in a vest and lungi unloads crates of fresh tomatoes, okra and coriander from a handcart, inspecting a tomato closely. Next, in the kitchen, a stout chef in his 50s with a white cap tastes a ladle of gravy and adds a pinch of masala from a steel dabba, frowning thoughtfully, a handwritten recipe card on the wall with crossed-out lines. Third, a narrow pass window where a young cook in an apron slides five plated thalis onto the counter at once, a wall clock above showing ten past one, steam rising. Far right, front of house, a smiling woman in her 30s in a maroon salwar kameez stands at the billing desk with an order pad, a table-number board and a small QR-code stand for UPI, customers seated at every table. Outside the building on the pavement, in the foreground, a lone home cook in a house-dress holds one frying pan and looks up at all four rooms with a worried face. Bright midday light, lively mood. Labels: "DATA" over the vegetable door, "FINE-TUNE" over the chef, "DEPLOY" over the billing desk.

key: Indian Railways does not just bu
name: ch00_railways_operations_dept
alt: A railway operations room where staff track coach numbers, maintenance logs, bookings and a punctuality board that is starting to slip.
scene: A wide view inside a busy railway operations office beside a station yard, large windows at the back showing a blue express train waiting on the tracks. Four desks run left to right. At the first, a middle-aged clerk in a cream shirt and spectacles chalks coach numbers onto a board showing which coach is attached to which train, a little coach-tag diagram beside it. At the second, a mechanic in navy overalls and a cap writes in a thick maintenance logbook open at a page with neat rows, a wrench and an oil can on the desk, so the same repair can be repeated exactly. At the third, a young woman in a sari works at a computer surrounded by towering stacks of reservation slips, the stacks reaching her shoulders to show crores of bookings. At the fourth, a senior officer in a white uniform with a whistle on a cord stands looking up at a large punctuality board where a line of green ticks slowly turns into amber and then red dots towards the right edge, his hand on his chin, concerned. In the foreground a passenger with a suitcase walks past unaware. Mid-morning light through dusty windows, calm but watchful. Labels: "VERSIONS" over the coach board, "LOGS" over the logbook, "DRIFT" next to the red dots on the punctuality board.

key: A ghostwriter for a busy CEO fir
name: ch00_ghostwriter_five_steps
alt: A ghostwriter at a desk surrounded by the five stages of the job: reading old posts, a reference folder, practice drafts, the boss choosing between two drafts, and a deadline calendar.
scene: A cosy home study seen from slightly above, a young ghostwriter (late 20s, kurta over jeans, round glasses) at the centre of a wooden desk, typing on a laptop. Around him, arranged clockwise like a story told around the desk, are the five stages of his job. Top left, a tall pile of printed articles and old blog posts tied with string, one held open in his left hand with sentences underlined. Top right, a fat lever-arch folder on a shelf labelled with tabs, a few pages pulled out and pinned to a corkboard for quick reference. Right side, a stack of practice drafts, the bottom ones heavily crossed out in red, the top one nearly clean. Bottom right, a small inset showing a busy executive in her 50s in a crisp blazer at her own desk, holding two drafts side by side and tapping one with a pen, smiling, the other put aside. Bottom left, a wall calendar with every Monday circled and a clock showing a deadline. A faint dotted loop connects the five stages around him. Warm evening lamp light, focused and productive mood. Labels: "RAG" on the folder, "FINE-TUNE" on the practice drafts, "PREFERENCE" above the executive choosing a draft.

key: Think of a bridge course at an e
name: ch00_bridge_course_two_directions
alt: An engineering college footbridge with two groups of students crossing in opposite directions, one carrying tools towards a theory hall and the other carrying books towards a workshop.
scene: A sunny engineering-college campus seen from the side, with a long covered footbridge stretching across a small canal between two buildings. On the left bank stands a noisy workshop with a lathe visible through an open shutter, sparks and oily workbenches. On the right bank stands a quiet lecture hall with a blackboard full of equations visible through a window. On the bridge, two groups walk in opposite directions and pass each other in the middle. Walking left to right, from the workshop towards the lecture hall, are three diploma holders in grease-stained work shirts carrying spanners and a multimeter, looking curiously at the blackboard ahead. Walking right to left, from the lecture hall towards the workshop, are three B.Sc. graduates in neat collared shirts carrying thick theory books and notebooks, peering eagerly at the machines ahead. In the very middle two of them, one from each group, exchange a friendly nod. A banner hangs from the bridge rail. A neem tree shades the left bank, and a few cycles are parked by the right building. Bright late-morning light, cheerful and hopeful mood. Labels: "ONE COURSE" on the bridge banner, "SOFTWARE" above the left group, "ML" above the right group.

key: Building a house in order: archi
name: ch00_house_build_eleven_stages
alt: A house being built in stages along a winding path, from architect's drawing to finished home handed to residents, with a dotted loop back to the start.
scene: A winding path drawn across the picture like a board game, with small scenes of building one Indian house in order, starting bottom left and ending top right. First, an architect in her 40s with a rolled blueprint sits at a drafting table. Next, a man collects a stamped permit at a municipal window beside a toolbox. Then trucks unload bricks, cement bags and steel rods. Then the same material is sorted into a godown with neatly labelled bays so a worker can fetch a bag fast. Then a foreman teaches two young masons how to lay bricks straight with a string line. Then an inspector in a hard hat checks a wall with a spirit level and a clipboard. Then masons pass bricks hand to hand efficiently up a ladder. Then a helper fetches exactly one bag of tiles from the godown at the moment a tiler asks. Then a smiling family of four receives a bunch of keys at the front gate of the finished yellow house with a mango tree. Finally a housing-society committee meets under a shamiana with a register. A dotted arrow loops from the committee back to the architect, to show the cycle starts again. Bright clear daylight, orderly and hopeful mood. Labels: "PLAN" at the architect, "KEYS" at the family, "LOOP" on the dotted arrow back to the start.

key: A new hire at a call centre. SFT
name: ch00_callcentre_four_tools
alt: A call-centre trainee shown in four small panels: studying a script manual, a supervisor comparing two calls, an audit score sheet, and a small cheat-sheet clipped onto the manual.
scene: A four-panel strip, two over two, following the same young call-centre trainee (early 20s, white shirt, ID lanyard, headset) through his first month in an open-plan office with rows of blue partitions. Top left: he sits with a thick ring-bound manual open at a page with rows of example lines in two columns, a customer speech bubble on one side and an agent bubble on the other, his finger following a row. Top right: a calm supervisor in her 40s in a green saree, sitting beside him, listens to two recorded calls on a dual-headphone splitter and holds up a card with a tick beside one call and a cross beside the other while he listens closely. Bottom left: a quality auditor at a separate desk scores a fixed list of ten test calls on a printed score sheet with a pencil, a stopwatch beside it. Bottom right: the same thick manual, untouched and closed, with one small yellow cheat-sheet card clipped to its front cover by a binder clip, the trainee smiling as he reads only the small card. Even office light, focused and supportive mood. Labels: "SFT" on the top-left manual, "PREFERENCE" on the supervisor card, "LORA" on the clipped cheat-sheet.

key: advanced batch: you should alrea
name: ch00_cricket_academy_entry
alt: Young players at the gate of a cricket academy's advanced batch, with a coach checking basic grip, fitness and match experience, while a distant stadium represents what they do not need yet.
scene: A cricket academy ground in the early morning, seen from the entrance gate. In the foreground a stern but kind coach in his 50s in a white tracksuit and cap holds a clipboard and checks three young players in whites lined up at the gate, each showing one thing. The first, a girl of about 16 with a ponytail, holds her bat with a correct, relaxed grip and a small rulebook tucked under her arm. The second, a lanky boy of about 17, has just finished shuttle runs between cones and is breathing hard but upright, a skipping rope over his shoulder. The third, a stocky boy of about 18, has grass stains on his trousers and a well-worn ball in his hand from playing matches on real grounds, a small inset bubble above him showing a dusty local maidan with a temporary boundary rope. Behind them, practice nets stretch across the ground with bowling machines. On the horizon, far away and slightly hazy, stands a huge floodlit stadium, clearly not part of today's entry check. Soft golden early light, fresh and encouraging mood. Labels: "PYTHON" above the girl with the correct grip, "ALGORITHMS" above the boy doing shuttle runs, "CLOUD" above the boy with the match-worn ball.

key: Opening a chai stall. Why: offic
name: ch01_chai_stall_why_what_how
alt: A new chai cart outside a metro station at 8 a.m., with office workers queueing and the owner managing a tiny menu, a gas cylinder, milk and a UPI code.
scene: Early morning outside a busy metro station exit, office workers in shirts and lanyards streaming out of the stairs at eight o'clock, a large station clock confirming the time. In the centre stands a brand-new pushcart chai stall, freshly painted green, run by a cheerful man in his 30s with a cotton towel over his shoulder, pouring masala chai from a height into small glasses. Left of the cart, a short queue of four office workers checks their watches; one young woman in a kurta and lanyard already sips with relief. On the cart itself, the menu board shows only two items, a chai glass and a biscuit jar, with two glass jars of biscuits beside it, nothing else. Under the cart, a red gas cylinder is tucked neatly; a teenage helper on a bicycle arrives from the right with two steel milk cans hanging from the handlebars; a printed UPI QR code is taped to the side of the cart. Dotted callout lines point to three areas. Soft golden early light, steam curling upward, busy but friendly mood. Labels: "WHY" in a bubble over the queue of office workers, "WHAT" over the two-item menu board, "HOW" pointing at the gas cylinder, milk cans and QR code together.

key: A good junior at a CA (chartered
name: ch01_ca_junior_draft_review
alt: A senior chartered accountant gives a short instruction to a junior who has read all past client letters; the junior returns a draft that the senior reads and signs.
scene: Inside a small chartered-accountant office with steel filing cabinets, ledgers on shelves and a calendar on the wall, shown as a three-step sequence from left to right across one wide picture. Left: a senior accountant in his 50s, grey moustache, white shirt and reading glasses on a cord, sits behind a teak desk and speaks a short instruction to a junior, a speech bubble showing a tiny envelope, a stern-but-polite face and a small book icon for last year's ruling. The junior, a bright woman of about 25 in a pale blue kurta, stands with a notebook, and behind her a tall cabinet bursts with years of his old client letters, several of which she has flagged with sticky notes. Middle: she types at her desk, a draft letter emerging on the screen whose handwriting-style font echoes the senior's own letters pinned beside the monitor. Right: back at the senior's desk, he reads the printed draft carefully with a red pen hovering over one line, about to sign at the bottom, a rubber stamp waiting beside it. Afternoon light through window blinds, calm professional mood. Labels: "INSTRUCTION" above the first speech bubble, "DRAFT" over the junior's screen, "REVIEW" above the senior reading with the pen.

key: A rubber stamp of your own signa
name: ch01_signature_stamp_drawer
alt: Three small scenes with a signature rubber stamp: a man stamping his own letters, a forged stamp of a neighbour's signature crossed out, and the stamp locked in a drawer.
scene: A triptych of three equal panels about one rubber stamp of a person's signature, each panel framed like a small window. Left panel: a man in his 40s in a checked half-sleeve shirt sits at his home desk stamping a neat pile of his own letters with a wooden-handled rubber stamp, an ink pad open beside him, looking pleased at how much time it saves, the stamped signature matching the name on the letterhead. Middle panel: a shifty-looking man in a cap tries to stamp a document with a second stamp carved with someone else's signature, while through the window an elderly neighbour in a dhoti waters plants unaware; the whole panel has a big red diagonal cross over it. Right panel: the first man turns a small key in the lock of his desk drawer, the original stamp and ink pad visible inside through a cut-away view, a key ring on his finger, the drawer firmly shut. A faint inset in the right panel's corner shows a speech bubble with fresh words stamped under his signature that he never wrote, with a small question mark. Even indoor light, serious but clear mood. Labels: "YOUR DATA" over the left panel, "FORGERY" over the middle panel, "RESTRICTED" over the locked drawer.

key: Ordering from a new restaurant e
name: ch01_new_restaurant_vs_tiffin
alt: Split scene: a man repeating his long food preferences to a new restaurant every day, versus a tiffin service that already has his preferences and past orders on file.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line, the same office worker (early 30s, glasses, striped shirt, slightly tired) in both halves. LEFT panel: at the counter of an unfamiliar restaurant, he leans forward and counts on his fingers while a long speech bubble overflows with small icons, a crossed-out oil drop, a crossed-out onion, three green chillies, and a small portrait of his mother in a kitchen. The waiter, a young man with a notepad, scratches his head; a wall calendar behind them shows the same scene repeating with tally marks for each day of the week. RIGHT panel: a doorstep where a friendly tiffin-service delivery woman in her 40s in a printed saree hands him a steel tiffin carrier; she holds a small notebook open to a page with his name, a little chilli icon, a crossed-out onion and a list of his past orders with ticks. He is smiling and not saying a word. Behind her, a bicycle with more stacked tiffin carriers. Warm lunchtime light, frustrated on the left and relaxed on the right. Labels: "EVERY TIME" over the left panel, "ON FILE" above the delivery woman's notebook.

key: Planning a family trip with a fi
name: ch01_family_trip_one_place
alt: A family around a dining table choosing one holiday destination from three, with a fixed budget envelope and a calendar showing one week of leave.
scene: A middle-class Indian dining room in the evening, a family of five gathered around a wooden table covered with travel brochures, viewed from a slight height. On the table lie three large travel posters: snowy mountains with a houseboat, a sunny beach with palm trees, and green backwaters with a canoe. The teenage daughter points eagerly at the mountains, the young son waves the beach poster, and the grandmother taps the backwaters one. At the head of the table the father (mid 40s, reading glasses pushed up on his forehead, kurta) holds a thin envelope of cash with a small rubber band, the budget, and the mother (early 40s, cotton saree) holds a wall calendar where one week is circled in red. In the centre of the table, the father has placed a pen tick on exactly one poster, the backwaters, while the other two are gently pushed to the edge. A small inset thought-bubble above the mother shows the chosen destination with a little extra ring of space around it, as if leaving room to add more later. Warm tube-light glow, lively family discussion that is settling into agreement. Labels: "BUDGET" on the envelope, "ONE WEEK" on the calendar, "MVP" on the ticked poster.

key: first day is serving batter with
name: ch01_dosa_cart_viable
alt: Two dosa carts: one serving only batter with an unready chutney grinder and confused customers, the other serving one complete plate of dosa, chutney and sambar to happy customers.
scene: A before-and-after split showing two dosa carts side by side on the same South Indian street corner, divided by a lamppost. LEFT: a cart where a nervous young vendor in a vest holds out a steel plate with only a ladle of raw batter on it, while behind him a chutney grinder sits unplugged with its lid open and a tangle of wire. Two customers, a college student with a backpack and an older man with an umbrella, stare at the plate with puzzled faces and are walking away. RIGHT: a second cart run by a confident woman in her 30s in a cotton saree with her hair tied back, flipping a golden crisp dosa on a hot tava with steam rising. She hands over a banana-leaf plate that holds one dosa, a small cup of coconut chutney and a cup of sambar. Three customers stand eating happily, one giving a thumbs-up, and the small menu board above her lists just one item with a tick. A small queue is forming. Bright morning light, tired on the left and cheerful on the right. Labels: "NOT VIABLE" above the left cart, "VIABLE" above the right cart, "SMALL BUT COMPLETE" on the right menu board.

key: Before designing your own house,
name: ch01_house_template_three_rooms
alt: An architect shows a young couple a standard house template with a kitchen, bedrooms and a bathroom joined by a corridor, while they customise colours without moving the essential rooms.
scene: A clean cut-away top-down view of a single-storey house model with the roof lifted off, sitting on a drawing table in an architect's office. The model follows a standard template: a kitchen with a stove, a steel spice box and a sink on the left; two bedrooms with beds and a cupboard in the middle; and a bathroom with a bucket and a tap on the right, all joined by one central corridor with little arrows showing how people walk between them. Beside the model lies a printed sheet of the same template, a simple plan of the three kinds of rooms. Around the table, a young couple in their late 20s plan their own version: the woman in a yellow kurta holds paint swatches against a bedroom wall, and the man in a T-shirt places a toy potted plant and a different floor tile into the kitchen, clearly customising decoration without moving any walls. An older architect in a grey kurta and spectacles taps the three room types on the printed template with a pencil, as if to say these must exist in every house. Soft daylight from a window, calm planning mood. Labels: "TEMPLATE" on the printed sheet, "MUST EXIST" over the three rooms, "YOUR CHOICE" over the paint swatches.

key: A wedding. The couple (the model
name: ch01_wedding_couple_and_vendors
alt: A wedding stage with the couple at the centre, surrounded by the many people who make the event work: caterers, decorators, a priest, sound, a guest list, parking and an envelope collector.
scene: A wide, high-angle view of a busy outdoor Indian wedding in a lawn at dusk, strings of marigold and fairy lights overhead. In the exact centre on a raised decorated stage stand the bride in a red lehenga and the groom in a cream sherwani, smiling, a small spotlight on them. All around them, in a ring, the people who make the event work are busy: left, a caterer in a white apron stirring a huge biryani handi over flames; behind the stage, two decorators on ladders tying flower strings; in front of the stage, a priest in saffron with a small sacred fire; right, a sound engineer in headphones at a mixing desk with big speakers; near the gate, a young man ticking names off a long guest list on a clipboard; at the far edge, an attendant with a torch waving cars into a parking lane; and beside the stage, an uncle at a small table collecting gift envelopes into a box. Thin dotted lines connect each helper to the stage, showing each hands something to the event. Warm golden evening light, festive mood. Labels: "MODEL" over the couple, "ML SYSTEM" in a banner above the whole lawn.

key: Monolith: a one-person dhaba whe
name: ch01_three_kitchens_designs
alt: Three kitchens side by side: a one-man dhaba, a restaurant where each customer must bring their own recipe card and spices, and a five-star kitchen manual too thick for a small restaurant.
scene: A triptych of three kitchens, each in its own panel. LEFT: a roadside dhaba where a single cook in his 40s in a vest buys vegetables from a basket, stirs a kadhai and serves a plate, all at once, three hands' worth of tasks drawn as motion lines; only a few plastic tables sit outside, and a queue beyond the tenth table is turned away. MIDDLE: a clean but empty modern restaurant kitchen whose shelves are completely bare; at the counter, a customer in a blazer has to hand over his own little spice tin and a handwritten recipe card along with his order, while the cook waits with empty hands, other customers in line behind him all clutching their own tins and cards. RIGHT: a young restaurant owner in a T-shirt sits on a stool in a tiny kitchen, overwhelmed, holding up a gigantic thick binder of a five-star hotel kitchen manual that is taller than he is, with dozens of coloured tabs. In a small inset at the bottom, a tray of food passes silently from one counter to the next with a slightly wrong spice in it, nobody noticing. Even indoor light, slightly comic mood. Labels: "MONOLITH" over the left, "STATELESS" over the middle, "TOO MUCH" over the right.

key: report-card office. Teachers
name: ch01_report_card_register
alt: A school office computing grades from teachers' raw marks into one register, which a scholarship committee and a parent-teacher meeting both read.
scene: Inside a school's records office with a ceiling fan and a big wooden almirah, shown as one flowing scene from left to right. On the left, three teachers, a man in a sweater vest and two women in sarees, drop bundles of raw mark-sheets into a wire tray on the counter. In the middle, an office clerk in his 50s with half-moon spectacles and a calculator copies each student's marks into a thick bound register, writing a percentage and a letter grade next to each roll number in neat columns; the register lies open under a desk lamp. Older register volumes stand on a shelf behind him, each spine marked with a different year. On the right, two groups read the very same open register: a scholarship committee of three people in formal clothes at a table, one tracing a line with a finger, and a parent-teacher meeting where a mother and a class teacher lean over it together. Both groups point to the same row. Late-afternoon light through barred windows, calm and orderly mood. Labels: "RAW MARKS" over the teachers' tray, "FEATURE STORE" over the register, "SAME NUMBERS" between the two reading groups.

key: A pharmacy that keeps each medic
name: ch01_pharmacy_batch_tracking
alt: A pharmacist checking a medicine batch number against a log listing manufacturing date and ingredient lots, tracing exactly what went into it.
scene: Inside a neat neighbourhood pharmacy with glass-fronted shelves of medicine boxes and a green cross sign glowing at the door. In the foreground, a careful pharmacist in her 40s in a white coat and dupatta holds up a strip of tablets to the light, reading a small printed batch number on the foil with a magnifying glass. On the counter in front of her lies an open ledger with columns, and a highlighted row shows the same batch number, a manufacturing date and three ingredient lot numbers. Thin dotted lines run from that row across the counter to three small sealed sacks on a back shelf, each tagged with a lot code, showing which ingredients went into this batch. Behind her, the shelves are organised by batch, each box with a small sticker. On the right, a worried customer, an elderly man in a woollen cap, holds a box and points at it, and she is reassuring him with a calm face because she can trace it. A small calendar on the wall marks the batch date. Clean white fluorescent light, careful and trustworthy mood. Labels: "BATCH" on the foil strip, "LINEAGE" over the dotted lines, "LOTS" over the three sacks.

key: A cricket team with batters, bow
name: ch01_cricket_coaches_independent
alt: Two cricket coaches working separately in different nets, the bowling coach and the batting coach, with both groups meeting only at the match.
scene: A large cricket training ground seen from a high angle, split into two practice areas by a low fence, with a match pitch at the far end. In the left practice net, a bowling coach in his 40s in a red tracksuit with a whistle demonstrates a new run-up to three young fast bowlers, marking footholds with small cones and a chalk line, ignoring everything on the other side. In the right practice net, a batting coach in her 30s in a navy tracksuit adjusts a young batter's stance with a bat, a ball machine behind them, completely focused on her own group. Neither coach looks at the other. At the far end of the ground, the two groups walk out from opposite sides onto the match pitch in white kits, the bowlers with a ball and the batters with bats, meeting at the stumps where an umpire in a white hat stands, the scoreboard ready. A dotted arrow from each net leads to the match pitch and nowhere else. Bright afternoon light, energetic and organised mood. Labels: "FEATURE" over the left net, "TRAINING" over the right net, "INTERFACE" over the match pitch.

key: A dabbawala sorting system. Tiff
name: ch01_dabbawala_sort_by_destination
alt: At a railway station, tiffins collected from many homes are sorted by destination code, not by home, while a collector from a new building joins the line with no change to the sorting.
scene: A busy suburban railway platform in the late morning, seen from slightly above. On the left, white-capped tiffin carriers in white kurta-pyjamas arrive from many directions carrying long wooden crates on their heads, each crate holding round steel tiffins of different shapes and with different cloth bags from many homes. In the centre, a large group squats on the platform floor sorting the tiffins quickly into groups, reading colourful painted letters and numbers on each lid and placing them by those codes into fresh crates, not by which home they came from. Several crates are clearly grouped by the same painted code. On the far right, the crates are loaded into the luggage compartment of a waiting train. At the bottom left, a new young collector, about 20, joins the arriving line from a freshly built tall apartment tower in the background, carrying just a few tiffins, while the sorters in the middle carry on exactly as before without looking up. Bright hazy light, purposeful rush. Labels: "MANY SOURCES" over the arriving carriers, "SORT BY CODE" over the sorting group, "NEW SOURCE" over the young collector.

key: buy a separate archive building.
name: ch01_library_boxed_snapshot
alt: A librarian pulls books from the main shelves by catalogue number into a box stamped with a date and batch number for a visiting training college, while readers keep using the same shelves.
scene: Inside a public library hall with tall wooden shelves and readers at long tables under ceiling fans. In the centre, a librarian in her 50s in a handloom saree and spectacles on a chain stands at a trolley, pulling books off the main shelves by reading small catalogue numbers on their spines, a printed list in her hand with ticks. She places them into a sturdy cardboard carton on the trolley. On the carton, a fresh ink stamp shows a date and a batch number. At the right edge, a young man from a training college in a blazer waits with a hand-truck to carry the stamped carton away, an earlier carton with a different date stamp already on his truck. On the left, ordinary readers continue using the same shelves, one young woman searching a shelf and another reading at the table, undisturbed. In the background, an empty plot seen through a window has a small sign showing a separate archive building that was never built. Soft daylight through tall windows, quiet and practical mood. Labels: "VECTOR DB" over the main shelves, "ARTIFACT" on the stamped carton, "TRAINING" over the waiting young man.

key: A new train coach design. Engine
name: ch01_coach_design_trials
alt: Railway coach prototypes going through experiments, testing against the current coach, a senior officer's sign-off, and then routine production at a factory.
scene: A long industrial scene inside a railway coach factory and test track, read left to right as four stages. First: an engineering shed where several engineers in hard hats and blue overalls examine three differently shaped coach prototypes on stands, one with a bent seat, one with odd windows, one sleek. Second: a test track where the best prototype, freshly painted, runs alongside the current standard coach on parallel rails while instruments on tripods record speed and vibration and a technician with a clipboard compares two graphs. Third: an office balcony overlooking the track where a senior railway officer in his 50s in a crisp white uniform with epaulettes signs a single form with a fountain pen, while a junior holds out the test report. Fourth: the factory floor at the far right, where identical copies of the approved coach roll out one after another in a line, workers waving, a calendar on the wall showing this happens every week. Bright daylight through high factory windows, careful and proud mood. Labels: "EXPERIMENTS" over the prototypes, "TESTS" over the test track, "APPROVAL" over the officer signing.

key: A customer-care call centre. The
name: ch01_callcentre_agent_inference
alt: A customer-care agent taking a call, pulling up past tickets on one screen, reading a script template on another, while a recorder captures the full call and the screens.
scene: A single customer-care desk in a call centre, seen from behind and slightly to the side so the agent and both her screens are visible. The agent, a calm young woman of about 26 with a headset and a lanyard, listens to a caller; a speech bubble from the headset shows a customer's question with a parcel icon. On her left screen, a stack of the customer's past tickets has been pulled up automatically, three cards fanned out, one of them clearly about something unrelated, a broken fan, with a small red question mark beside it. On her right screen, a script template with blank slots is being filled in with the ticket details. Between the screens, a small desk microphone and a recording box with a red light labelled with a cassette icon records everything, and a thin cable runs from the box to a server rack in the background where a supervisor in a sweater reviews recordings that include both the call and what was on the screens. Even office light with blue partitions, efficient but watchful mood. Labels: "RETRIEVAL" over the left screen, "PROMPT" over the right screen, "MONITORING" on the recording box.

key: Before a long cooking session, a
name: ch02_cook_mise_en_place
alt: A home cook preparing everything before cooking: checking the gas cylinder, filling the spice box, sharpening knives and fitting a pressure-cooker gasket.
scene: A bright Indian home kitchen in the morning, seen from the doorway, before any cooking has started. At the centre a capable woman in her 40s in a cotton nightie-style house dress with a dupatta tied at the waist moves through her preparation. Four small moments are shown around her at once, like a clock face. Top left, she crouches to check the red gas cylinder under the counter, turning the regulator knob with a small spanner. Top right, she fills a round steel masala dabba, each of its seven small bowls being topped up with turmeric, chilli, jeera and mustard seeds from labelled jars. Bottom right, she sharpens a kitchen knife on a sharpening stone, three more knives lined up beside it. Bottom left, she presses a new rubber gasket into the lid of a pressure cooker. The stove is unlit and no pot is cooking yet, and a printed recipe card leans against the wall with nothing ticked off. In a small inset bubble at the top, a future version of her cooks a full meal smoothly without stopping to look for anything. Fresh morning light through a window grille, calm and ready mood. Labels: "SETUP" over the whole scene, "PINNED VERSIONS" on the gasket box, "READY" in the inset bubble.

key: Speed-dial on an old phone: pres
name: ch02_speed_dial_phone
alt: An elderly man pressing one key on an old phone to call home, with a sticker showing what the key means, mapping a long phone number to a single button.
scene: A close, warm scene in a small living room with a crocheted doily on a side table. An elderly man in his 70s in a white kurta and thick-rimmed glasses sits in a cane chair holding an old push-button mobile phone, his thumb pressing one large key. Above the phone, a thought bubble shows a very long string of digits fading out because he no longer needs to remember it. Taped to the back of the phone is a small paper sticker written by hand with two short lines, a key number with a tiny house and another key number with a tiny office building. A dotted line runs from the pressed key to a small picture of a house where a woman picks up her phone and smiles. On the side table, his granddaughter (about 12, school uniform) holds up the phone's settings screen to show him that the full number is still written there, anyone can open and read it. On the wall behind, a calendar and a framed family photo. Soft evening lamp light, gentle and cosy mood. Labels: "ONE KEY" over the pressed button, "LONG COMMAND" over the fading digits, "STILL READABLE" over the open settings screen.

key: A model registry is like the rec
name: ch02_court_record_room
alt: A district court record room where a clerk retrieves exactly one numbered judgment file with its full papers and a summary sheet, and a public record room next door open to visitors.
scene: Inside a high-ceilinged district court record room with tall steel racks stacked with red cloth-bound bundles, each tied with string and tagged with a case number. In the foreground, an old record-keeper in his 60s in a khaki uniform and a white cap stands at a wooden counter and hands over exactly one bundle to a young lawyer in a black coat and white bands. The bundle is opened to show three parts: a thick stack of papers, a page of settings and notes, and a single crisp summary sheet clipped on top. The tag on the bundle reads "2024/117", and the lawyer holds a requisition slip with the same number. A rack beside them shows other bundles with numbers in sequence. Through an open archway on the right, a second room is visible with its door wide open and a board at the entrance, where ordinary members of the public, a student and a retired man, browse freely among racks. Shafts of dusty light from high windows, quiet and orderly mood. Labels: "MODEL REGISTRY" above the counter, "MODEL CARD" on the summary sheet, "PUBLIC" over the open archway.

key: A phone charger with swappable p
name: ch02_charger_swappable_heads
alt: One phone charger with three swappable plug heads for different countries, a traveller clipping on the right head at each stop.
scene: A traveller's desk in a hotel room, seen from above, with a passport, a boarding pass and an open suitcase at the edge. In the centre lies one white phone charger body with a cable, the same body throughout. Fanned out beside it are three detachable plug heads: an Indian round-pin head, a UK three-square-pin head and a US flat-pin head, each with a small flag-coloured band but no writing. A young woman traveller in her late 20s with a backpack and a scarf clips the UK head onto the charger body, her fingers pressing it in place with a click shown by small motion lines. Above the desk, three small inset circles show the same charger body plugged into three different wall sockets in three different hotel rooms, with only the head changing each time. In the corner of the desk, a small extra device with an unusual cable lies apart, with a question mark, suggesting some places still need special setup. Warm morning light through curtains, practical and relaxed mood. Labels: "SAME CODE" on the charger body, "STACK" over the three plug heads, "SPECIAL SETUP" next to the odd device.

key: A restaurant kitchen (the llm_en
name: ch02_kitchen_two_counters
alt: A restaurant kitchen serving through two counters, a dine-in waiter and a delivery counter, with every dish packed into standard boxes and one odd dish needing a custom box.
scene: A cut-away view of a restaurant with one shared kitchen in the middle and two serving points on either side. In the kitchen, two cooks in white aprons follow the same recipes on a board, stirring curries and rolling rotis, unchanged. To the left, a dining room where a smiling waiter in a black waistcoat carries plates on a tray to a family at a table. To the right, a small delivery counter facing a side lane where a delivery rider in a helmet and a reflective jacket waits on a scooter with an insulated bag. On the delivery counter, a packer in her 30s slides dishes into identical standard rectangular containers, stacked neatly. Next to her, one awkward dish, a tall layered dessert on a stand, does not fit any standard container, so she is folding a special custom box around it with tape, looking amused. A small inset at the top shows the same dishes being cooked in two separate kitchens far apart, linked by a dotted arrow, to suggest each step may run in a different place. Warm evening light, busy but organised mood. Labels: "PIPELINES" over the dine-in side, "REST API" over the delivery counter, "MATERIALIZER" on the custom box.

key: Courier parcels with a printed l
name: ch02_courier_parcel_label
alt: A courier sorting office where parcels are routed by reading printed labels with sender, weight, contents and a tracking number, without opening the boxes.
scene: A busy courier sorting office seen from a raised platform, with conveyor belts and wire cages labelled by city. In the foreground, a close view of one brown parcel on the belt with a large printed label showing a sender line, a small weight figure, a contents line "2 books", a barcode and a long tracking number. A sorter in his 30s in a company polo shirt and cap scans the label with a handheld scanner and, without opening the box, pushes it onto the correct branch of the belt with a flick, an arrow showing its route to a cage. Further along the belt, a row of near-identical parcels from the same sender carries small stickers with an increasing sequence number, the tenth one highlighted. At the back, a supervisor at a desk looks at a screen listing labels in rows. To one side, a parcel with an almost blank label sits in a separate tray with a question mark, because nobody added the useful fields. Bright fluorescent light, efficient and orderly mood. Labels: "METADATA" next to the large label, "UUID" under the tracking number, "VERSION" over the row of numbered parcels.

key: A pressure cooker is the pipelin
name: ch02_pressure_cooker_recipe_cards
alt: One pressure cooker used for rajma or chana by swapping recipe cards, with a file of every used card kept so last Sunday's batch can be traced.
scene: A homely kitchen counter in close view. In the centre sits one large steel pressure cooker on a gas stove, its whistle letting off a small puff of steam. Pinned on a little stand right beside the cooker is a recipe card showing a bowl of rajma, a soaking time, a pinch of masala and three whistle marks. A man in his late 30s in a T-shirt and apron is in the middle of swapping it for a second card showing chana and five whistle marks, holding the new card in one hand and the old one in the other, while the cooker itself stays exactly where it is. On the shelf above, a thick ring binder lies open, filled with used recipe cards in plastic sleeves, each dated, and his young daughter (about 9) points to one sleeve marked with last Sunday's date, a small photo of that day's rajma bowl beside it. Behind them, jars of dals and beans stand in a neat row. A small inset shows the cooker with a padlock icon on its body, because the card cannot change the cooker itself. Soft daytime light, homely and methodical mood. Labels: "PIPELINE" on the cooker, "CONFIG" on the recipe card, "RUN HISTORY" on the binder.

key: analyst who records every net se
name: ch02_cricket_analyst_net_sessions
alt: A cricket team analyst recording every net session on a laptop, and the coach comparing sessions by the same numbers when choosing the team.
scene: A cricket practice ground in the late afternoon. In the background, a bowler in whites runs in towards a batter in a net, a speed gun on a tripod beside the net. In the foreground, a team analyst in her late 20s in a team polo and cap sits at a folding table under an umbrella with a laptop, a notebook and a fitness-band charger, recording every ball: a spreadsheet on the screen has rows with columns for bowler, ball type, pitch, speed, line and length, and a small rising and falling line chart next to it. Beside the table, a stand holds a few fitness trackers blinking. On the right, the head coach, a grey-haired man in his 50s in a team tracksuit, leans over her shoulder and compares two sessions side by side on the screen with a finger, while a whiteboard behind him shows an empty team list of eleven numbered slots being filled in. On the left, a clipboard of rough handwritten notes from memory lies discarded on the grass. Warm late-afternoon light, focused and analytical mood. Labels: "HYPERPARAMETERS" over the spreadsheet columns, "LOSS CURVE" on the small chart, "SYSTEM METRICS" on the fitness trackers.

key: An IRCTC PNR status page. One PN
name: ch02_pnr_journey_timeline
alt: A railway enquiry clerk opening one passenger's journey record that shows each event in order, contrasted with a mountain of unsorted event slips for the whole railway.
scene: A split composition at a railway reservation office. LEFT, the larger part: a helpful clerk in her 40s in a blue uniform saree sits at a computer behind a glass counter, and a worried passenger in his 30s with a suitcase stands before her holding a printed ticket with a ten-digit number. On her screen, and drawn large above the counter like a vertical timeline, one record for that number unfolds as a tree of events in order: booking, a waitlist number moving from 12 to 3, chart prepared, final berth confirmed, with small icons beside each, and two short side-branches showing a retry. RIGHT, a smaller panel: a junior clerk is buried up to his chest in a heap of thousands of tiny paper event slips from the whole railway, all mixed together, searching with a magnifying glass for one passenger's slips and looking defeated. A dotted line from the passenger's ticket number goes straight to the neat timeline on the left. Bright office lighting, relieved on the left and exhausted on the right. Labels: "TRACE" over the neat timeline, "FLAT LOGS" over the heap of slips.

key: A big steel almirah where each f
name: ch02_almirah_vs_medicine_cabinet
alt: A family steel almirah where each member stores things their own way, beside a medicine cabinet with fixed labelled slots.
scene: A bedroom in an Indian home, with two pieces of storage side by side against a pale green wall. LEFT: a tall grey steel almirah with both doors open. Each shelf belongs to a different family member and is organised differently: the mother's shelf has silk saris folded with paper tags; the father's shelf has files in clear plastic folders; the teenage son's shelf has a jumble of cricket gear, a cap and a few comic books; the grandmother's shelf has small cloth bundles tied with string. Each shelf has a small name card. A daughter of about 10 pulls a folder from her father's shelf easily, finding it by owner. RIGHT: a white wall-mounted medicine cabinet with a glass door, divided into identical small slots, each with a printed label and holding exactly one kind of item in the same way. A grandfather in a vest and spectacles places a strip of tablets into the right slot. Between the two, a young man in his 20s holds a small notebook with a checklist, looking at the almirah with a slight frown, as if planning to add some order. Soft daylight, homely mood. Labels: "DOCUMENTS" over the almirah, "SQL TABLE" over the cabinet, "ODM" on the young man's checklist.

key: A library. MongoDB is the stack
name: ch02_library_stack_and_map
alt: A library where donated books are stored as received in a back stack room, while a librarian at the front helps a reader by meaning, pointing to a shelf of related topics.
scene: A small town library seen as a cut-away of two connected rooms. LEFT: a dim back stack room where donated books of every size lie on shelves exactly as received, some still tied with string and with donor slips sticking out, a helper in his 20s carrying in a fresh carton. RIGHT: the bright front reading room where an experienced librarian in her 50s with silver hair and a shawl listens to a farmer in his 40s in a turban and kurta who describes, with his hands, what he needs. A thought bubble above her head shows a soft map of the room with glowing clusters: a cluster of books with rain clouds and crop icons sits right next to a cluster about canals and pumps. She points confidently to a shelf where monsoon farming and irrigation books stand side by side, though no title matches his exact words. A dotted arrow runs from his speech bubble to that shelf. A narrow doorway joins the two rooms, with a cart passing through. Warm afternoon light through tall windows, helpful mood. Labels: "RAW STORE" over the stack room, "VECTOR DB" over the librarian's map bubble, "BY MEANING" on the dotted arrow.

key: The root account is the owner of
name: ch02_housing_society_keys
alt: A housing society's owner with all keys, a staff member with a small key ring, a watchman given a master key to an empty flat, and a UPI ID beside a hidden PIN.
scene: The entrance lobby of a new apartment building, shown as one scene with several characters. On the left, the society owner, a dignified man in his 60s in a Nehru jacket, holds a huge iron ring with every key, standing beside a locked steel cabinet. In the middle, a young maintenance staff member in a uniform shirt carries a small key ring with only three keys, for the pump room, terrace and meter room, each with a coloured tag. On the right, a watchman in a khaki uniform and cap receives a single big master key from the owner, and through an open door behind him an empty, unfurnished test flat is visible with bare walls; a small inset beside it shows the same key in a fully occupied building with a warning triangle. In the foreground at the bottom, a large printed card shows a visible UPI ID beside a PIN field covered by a hand, with dots instead of digits. A tiny inset in the corner shows rows of glowing machines with a rising bill, the danger of a stolen key. Even daylight, careful mood. Labels: "ROOT" over the owner, "ADMIN" over the master key, "SECRET" over the covered PIN.

key: A fully serviced co-working spac
name: ch02_coworking_gpu_desk
alt: A serviced co-working space where a developer brings only a laptop while the space provides desks, power, internet and cleaning, plus a rented reception desk answering visitors.
scene: A modern serviced co-working floor with large windows, plants and long shared desks. In the centre, a young developer in his late 20s in a hoodie walks in carrying only a slim laptop and a coffee cup, sitting at a desk that already has power sockets, an ethernet cable, a monitor and a desk lamp ready. Around him, the space quietly provides everything else: a facilities worker in a grey uniform mops the floor; an IT technician adjusts a router rack visible through a glass wall, where rows of powerful machines with small fans hum; a staff member brings water bottles. At the front, a reception desk with a cheerful receptionist in her 20s with a headset greets a visitor at any hour, a clock above showing nearly midnight with the city dark outside. Off to the side, a second rented desk stands completely empty with a large running meter mounted on it, the dial turning, and no one sitting there. Cool evening light from the windows mixed with warm desk lamps, efficient mood. Labels: "MANAGED" over the whole floor, "ENDPOINT" over the reception desk, "IDLE COST" over the empty desk with the meter.

key: Three ways to get lunch at work.
name: ch02_three_ways_lunch
alt: Three ways to get lunch at work: ordering from a delivery app menu, cooking in a rented equipped kitchen, or building your own kitchen with gas, plumbing and chimney.
scene: A triptych of three panels with the same office worker, a woman in her early 30s in a pastel shirt with an ID card, solving lunch in three different ways. LEFT panel: at her office desk she taps a phone showing a food-delivery menu with only six fixed dishes, and a delivery rider is already handing over a sealed bag at the door; she looks relaxed but scrolls in vain for a dish that is not on the menu. MIDDLE panel: in a rented, fully equipped commercial kitchen with gleaming stoves, she cooks her own special dish in an apron, while a landlord in a vest stands at the door holding a rent bill even though half the week's calendar on the wall shows days she didn't come. RIGHT panel: in an unfinished room, she wears a hard hat and works with a plumber and a gas fitter installing a gas line, a sink and a chimney hood, sweating but satisfied, and a stack of many meal boxes in the corner shows she can feed the whole office cheaply once it's done. Bright midday light, light-hearted mood. Labels: "MENU ONLY" over the left panel, "RENTED KITCHEN" over the middle, "OWN KITCHEN" over the right panel.

key: A kirana shop shelves goods by t
name: ch03_kirana_shelves_by_type
alt: A kirana shopkeeper shelving goods by type, rice, oil and soap, regardless of which wholesaler delivered them, with a new supplier's rice going onto the same rice shelf.
scene: Inside a small, crowded kirana shop seen from just inside the doorway, with a wooden counter, a weighing scale and a calculator in the foreground. Behind the counter, three tall shelves are clearly grouped by kind of goods: one full of rice sacks of different colours, one of oil tins and bottles, one of soap bars and detergent packets. The owner, a friendly man in his 50s with a moustache and a vest under an open shirt, carries a new sack of rice from a fresh supplier's handcart at the right edge, a young delivery boy in a cap still standing beside the cart, and places it straight onto the rice shelf next to sacks from two other suppliers with differently coloured printed bags. The shelf labels and the billing counter stay exactly as they are. On each sack, a small paper tag hangs on a string, showing where it came from and a little link icon, so the source is still known without changing the shelf. In the background, a customer in a sari waits at the counter with a cloth bag. Warm midday light through the shutter, busy but tidy mood. Labels: "BY TYPE" over the shelves, "NEW SOURCE" over the fresh supplier's cart, "PLATFORM TAG" on the small hanging tags.

key: A small family business keeping
name: ch03_files_cupboard_to_software
alt: A family business moving from a cupboard of labelled paper files to accounting software when invoices grow into lakhs, with a small interface panel between the staff and the storage.
scene: A before-and-after picture of the same small family business office, split diagonally. LEFT, earlier: a modest office with a single wooden cupboard of labelled box files, a few hundred bills inside, and a cheerful father in his 50s in a safari suit pulling out the right file in seconds, his teenage daughter watching. RIGHT, years later: the same office now overflowing, with towers of invoices on every chair and the floor, and a chartered accountant in a grey blazer holding a chart of quarterly figures and gesturing at a computer screen showing accounting software. The now-grown daughter, in her late 20s in a formal kurta, sits at the computer carrying bundles from the cupboard to the screen, while the father looks relieved. Between the staff and the storage, on a small wall-mounted panel, there is a single neat request window through which everyone asks for files, so when the storage changes behind it nobody else's routine has to change. A calendar on the wall shows the years passing. Daylight in the left half and tube-light glow in the right half, a feeling of growth. Labels: "SMALL DATA" over the cupboard, "AT SCALE" over the software screen, "INTERFACE" on the request window.

key: A railway control chart: each tr
name: ch03_railway_control_chart
alt: A railway control room with a large chart showing each train's slot, departure and arrival times and what it carried, with an officer looking up one exact past run.
scene: A railway control room at a junction station, viewed from behind two controllers at their desks. Covering the back wall is a giant control chart: horizontal lines for time and several coloured diagonal lines, each one a train, with small boxes along each line noting departure time, arrival time and a cargo icon such as grain sacks or coal. Each train's line is like one step in a sequence, linked to the next by a short hand-off. In the foreground, a senior controller in his 50s in a white uniform shirt with a lanyard holds a phone receiver and puts his finger on one specific box on a printed copy of last Tuesday's chart, while a passenger complaint form lies on his desk next to it. Beside him, a younger controller in her 30s writes the next train's departure time into a log. Through a window at the side, a goods train passes slowly on the tracks. A small inset on the right shows the same chart being started three different ways: a hand pressing a button, a clock, and a bell, to hint that runs can be triggered by hand, schedule or event. Cool fluorescent light, precise and calm mood. Labels: "STEP" over one train line, "ARTIFACTS" over the cargo icons, "RUN HISTORY" over the printed old chart.

key: The enquiry counter at a big rai
name: ch03_enquiry_counter_dispatcher
alt: A station enquiry clerk reading only the start of each ticket and pointing passengers to their platform, sending an oddly printed ticket to the general waiting hall.
scene: A large Indian railway station concourse with high arched ceilings and display boards. In the centre, an enquiry counter with a glass window where a quick, no-nonsense clerk in his 40s with a pencil behind his ear glances only at the first line of each ticket held up to the glass. A short queue faces him. The first passenger, a student with a backpack, gets a pointing finger towards a platform sign on the left showing a train icon. The second passenger, a woman in a sari with a small child, is pointed towards a different platform on the right. The third passenger, an older man in a cap, holds a ticket printed in an unusual small font with the first characters slightly different, and the clerk, without reading further, points him to a large door marked by a bench icon, the general waiting hall, where several confused passengers already sit with similar odd tickets. A magnifying-glass inset shows the clerk's eye looking only at the first few characters of a ticket. Morning light through high windows, crowded but orderly mood. Labels: "DISPATCHER" over the clerk, "DEFAULT" over the waiting-hall door, "PATTERN MATCH" on the magnifying-glass inset.

key: An Instagram reel binge with a s
name: ch03_scroll_stop_rule
alt: A young man scrolling a short-video app with a rule to stop after five swipes or when the feed says caught up, and each swipe waiting for the next item to load.
scene: A close view of a young man in his early 20s lying on a bed in a hostel room, a phone held above his face, a cup of tea going cold on the side table and a clock showing late night. On the phone screen, a vertical feed of short videos is mid-swipe, with a small loading spinner where the next video is about to appear. Above the phone, five small circles hover like a counter, four already filled and the fifth empty, showing his self-imposed limit. Beside it, a second small badge shows a tick with the words "all caught up", the other way to stop. A sticky note on the wall above his bed has a hand-drawn rule with the number 5 circled. In a small inset at the bottom right, the same phone shows a page that suddenly grows taller because a banner advertisement has just loaded at the bottom, with a ruler measuring its height and a confused question mark beside it, hinting that page height can change for unrelated reasons. Dim blue phone light on his face and a warm table lamp, relaxed but disciplined mood. Labels: "SCROLL LIMIT" over the five circles, "WAIT TO LOAD" next to the spinner, "HEIGHT CHECK" on the inset ruler.

key: Ordering a thali at any roadside
name: ch03_dhaba_thali_vs_home
alt: Split scene: a fast roadside dhaba thali that cannot be customised versus home cooking where the cook controls every ingredient.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line, the same young man in his late 20s in a checked shirt in both halves. LEFT panel: at a busy highway dhaba with charpais and a big tandoor, a waiter swiftly sets down a steel thali with dal, sabzi, rotis and rice in front of him, only moments after he sat down; he looks pleased at the speed but raises one hand to ask for less salt in the dal, and the waiter is already walking away, a shrug in his shoulders. A small inset shows three different dhabas along the highway, each thali looking a bit different. RIGHT panel: in a small home kitchen, the same man in an apron stands at the stove with sleeves rolled up, measuring a small spoon of salt very precisely, with fresh vegetables, a spice box and a recipe notebook laid out, sweating a little; a wall clock shows that this took much longer, but he tastes the dal with a satisfied nod. Warm afternoon light on the left and soft evening light on the right, contrasting quick convenience with full control. Labels: "READY HELPER" over the left panel, "CUSTOM CRAWLER" over the right panel.

key: Sending a junior to a government
name: ch03_junior_copies_form_boxes
alt: A junior clerk at a government office who queues to log in, flips through every page of a file and copies only two boxes, coming back with blanks when the form is redesigned.
scene: A three-step strip inside a crowded government office with ceiling fans, steel almirahs and tall stacks of files tied with red tape. Step one, left: a young junior in his early 20s in a light shirt with a satchel stands in a long queue in front of a window marked with a token number and shows an ID card to a clerk, getting a stamp on his pass. Step two, centre: seated on a bench, he flips through a thick file page by page with his thumb, motion lines showing the scrolling, until he reaches a printed form. He copies exactly two boxes from it, a name box and a subject box, into his small notebook, his finger on each box. Step three, right: a different day, the same office now has a redesigned form where those two boxes have moved to new places on the page, and the junior, not noticing, copies from the old positions and walks back to his boss with a notebook whose two lines are empty, a calm but blank face, while the boss in a waistcoat frowns. Fluorescent light and dust in the air, routine mood. Labels: "LOG IN" over the queue, "SCROLL" over the flipping file, "NONE" on the blank notebook lines.

key: behind it, the app builds the ba
name: ch03_upi_app_vs_neft_form
alt: Split scene: a woman paying with one tap on a UPI app while the bank work happens hidden behind it, versus a man filling a long bank transfer form by hand.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: in a vegetable market, a young woman in her late 20s in a kurta with a cloth bag taps a single button on her phone to pay a vendor, a sabziwala who smiles at the ding on his small speaker. Behind her phone, a transparent cut-away bubble reveals the hidden machinery she doesn't see: tiny gears, folded bank messages, a wax-seal style signature and a small loop arrow for retries, all happening automatically. RIGHT panel: inside a bank branch, an older man in his 50s in a sleeveless sweater and glasses sits at a writing desk with a pen chained to it, carefully filling a long paper transfer form with many boxes, account number, branch code, amount in words, with a second spare form beside him because he made a mistake on the first; a queue forms behind him. In a small inset at the bottom of the left panel, the woman lifts the phone cover to peek at the actual message being sent, for when something odd happens. Bright daylight on the left and fluorescent bank light on the right, easy versus laborious mood. Labels: "ODM" over the left panel, "RAW QUERIES" over the right panel, "PEEK" on the inset.

key: A school register: every student
name: ch03_school_register_streams
alt: A school register where every row shares roll number, name and class, with the science stream adding a lab group column and commerce adding an accounts elective column, all in the same binding.
scene: A close, slightly overhead view of a large bound school register lying open on a teacher's wooden desk, the binding and page layout clearly the same on both pages. On every row, the first three columns are the same and printed in the same style: roll number, name and class. The left page belongs to the science stream and has one extra column at the end for lab group, with entries like small flask icons and group letters. The right page belongs to the commerce stream and has a different extra column for accounts elective, with small ledger icons. A teacher in her 40s in a cotton saree and spectacles writes a new row on the science page with a fountain pen, while a student in a white uniform stands beside the desk spelling his name. A thin ruler lies across the shared columns, linking both pages, and a small brass clip at the top marks the common binding. In a small corner inset, a row with a misspelled name is accepted without complaint, showing the register checks the shape of each row but not whether the entry is true. Soft morning classroom light, orderly mood. Labels: "BASE DOCUMENT" over the shared columns, "SUBCLASS" over each extra column, "TYPES ONLY" on the inset.

key: A school bus with one route shee
name: ch03_school_bus_route_sheets
alt: One school bus with a different route sheet for each child, and a conductor filing a slip after each trip listing stops and pickups.
scene: A yellow school bus parked at a school gate in the early morning, seen from the side with its door open. Inside the doorway, a cheerful conductor in his 40s in a khaki uniform and a cap holds a clipboard holding several separate route sheets, each one a small map with dotted stops and a child's photo at the top, and he is flipping to the next sheet. Three children of different ages with school bags and water bottles wait in line, each holding up a matching coloured card. The bus itself, its driver and its engine stay the same throughout. On the right, a small wooden box hangs by the school gate, where the conductor has just dropped a filed slip from his last trip, the slip visible with a short line showing a stop count matching a pickup count, "26 stops, 26 pickups". In a small inset at the top, two identical buses leave the depot one after another with different route sheets, hinting at runs that can go back to back. Clear early-morning light with long shadows, routine and dependable mood. Labels: "PIPELINE" on the side of the bus, "CONFIG" on the route sheets, "RUN REPORT" on the filed slip.

key: app crashes on one route, so you
name: ch03_ride_crash_auto_metro
alt: A commuter whose ride app crashes on one stretch, who takes an auto-rickshaw for that part, and as a backup takes the metro for the whole trip, while a planned route remains unlearned.
scene: A city map drawn as a cheerful top-down illustration with a commuter's journey shown as three alternatives. A young man in his late 20s with a laptop bag stands at the start point, a residential gate, holding a phone whose screen shows a cracked error symbol from a ride app. Path one: a road leading through the city, where for one red-marked stretch he hops into a green-and-yellow auto-rickshaw with a friendly driver, then continues on, the stretch dotted to show he skipped it differently. Path two: a straight elevated metro line in blue running from a station near the start directly to the office tower at the destination, with the same man sitting comfortably inside a metro coach reading. Path three: the original planned road route drawn faintly with small question marks along it, never actually travelled. At the destination, an office tower, he arrives on time, but a thought bubble above him shows that faint route with a puzzled face, because he still doesn't know whether it works. Bright morning light, practical and slightly wry mood. Labels: "SKIP LINKS" over the auto-rickshaw stretch, "BACKUP DATA" over the metro line, "UNTESTED" over the faint route.

key: An LLM is a brilliant lawyer who
name: ch04_lawyer_and_junior_files
alt: A senior lawyer who stopped reading the news years ago, reasoning at his desk while his junior places the latest relevant case files in front of him before a client meeting.
scene: A wood-panelled lawyer's chamber with shelves of old law books, a ceiling fan and a window showing a court building. At the centre sits a senior advocate in his 60s in a black coat, white bands and silver hair, thoughtful and articulate, gesturing with a fountain pen as he reasons through a case. On the wall behind him, a calendar is frozen on an old date with a cobweb on its corner, and a pile of yellowed, unopened newspapers lies on a side table, showing he stopped reading the news long ago. Rushing in from the right is his junior, a sharp woman of about 27 in a black coat with her hair tied back, carrying a stack of crisp new case files tied with pink tape, fresh dates visible on their covers, and placing the top three files on his desk under the lamp. One of the files on the desk is subtly wrong, with a different colour cover and a small red question mark, hinting that a wrong file leads to a confident wrong answer. At the doorway, a client in a business shirt waits with a briefcase. Warm lamplight on old wood, serious but hopeful mood. Labels: "LLM" over the senior lawyer, "RETRIEVAL" over the junior with the files, "CONTEXT" on the files on his desk.

key: An open-book exam versus a close
name: ch04_open_vs_closed_book_exam
alt: Split scene: a student in a closed-book exam confidently writing a guessed date, and a student in an open-book exam quoting a page number that the examiner checks.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line, both halves set in the same high-school examination hall with long wooden desks and a large clock. LEFT panel: a boy of about 16 in a white uniform shirt writes quickly in his answer sheet with a confident smile, while a thought bubble above him shows a fuzzy calendar with a big question mark, because he has forgotten the actual date and is guessing. No books are on his desk. RIGHT panel: a girl of about 16 in the same uniform has a thick textbook open beside her answer sheet at a page with a visible number, "page 47", and she copies the relevant line with a finger on it, writing the page number in her answer. Behind her, a stern examiner in his 50s in a grey safari suit leans over with spectacles and checks the page number against her answer, nodding. In a small inset at the bottom of the right panel, another student flips through his allowed book and finds the topic missing, writing a short honest line instead. Bright morning light through tall windows, tense but fair mood. Labels: "CLOSED BOOK" over the left panel, "OPEN BOOK" over the right panel, "CITE THE PAGE" by the examiner.

key: A railway enquiry counter. Overn
name: ch04_enquiry_clerk_timetable_binder
alt: A railway enquiry clerk who receives an updated timetable binder overnight, then answers a passenger's question by flipping to the right pages and reading them with the question in mind.
scene: A two-part scene at a railway enquiry counter. In the upper left, a small night-time inset: a back-office worker in a cardigan under a desk lamp slides freshly printed pages into a fat ring-binder timetable, a clock on the wall showing past midnight. The main scene, daytime: the enquiry counter behind a glass window, with a station clock and a crowd in the background. A traveller in her 30s with a trolley bag leans to the speaking hole and asks a question, a speech bubble showing a train icon, a question mark and a city skyline. The clerk, a middle-aged man in a blue uniform with half-moon glasses, has the binder open and flips quickly to the right section, a few pages lifting in motion; two pages are highlighted with a soft glow, one of them clearly about a different city that only looks similar. He reads those pages with the question floating faintly above them, and his own speech bubble answers with a clock time and a platform number. Arrows link the steps: from the binder pages to his eyes, and from his eyes to his answer. Bright daylight, helpful mood. Labels: "INGESTION" over the night inset, "RETRIEVE" over the flipping pages, "GENERATE" over the clerk's answer.

key: Making a library catalogue. Coll
name: ch04_library_catalogue_cards
alt: A library cataloguing line: collecting donated books, wiping stickers off, cutting topics into index cards, giving each card a shelf code, and filing them with title, page and date.
scene: A long wooden table running across a library workroom, viewed from the side, with five volunteers working along it left to right like an assembly line. First, an old man in a kurta lifts donated books out of a cardboard carton. Second, a young woman in a T-shirt with a damp cloth wipes off price stickers and pencil scribbles from a book cover. Third, a college student with headphones around his neck cuts a long printed page into neat strips and pastes each strip onto its own index card, one topic per card. Fourth, a librarian in her 40s with a bun stamps each card with a shelf code using a numbered stamp, and a small inset beside her shows the code as a short row of many tiny numbers instead of one word. Fifth, a teenager files the cards into a wooden drawer cabinet, each card with a small corner note showing a title, a page number and a date. Behind them, a wall map of the shelves shows cards with similar topics placed near each other with dotted circles. Warm afternoon light, steady productive mood. Labels: "CLEAN" over the wiping step, "CHUNK" over the card cutting, "EMBED" over the shelf-code stamp.

key: Two people pointing at the sky f
name: ch04_terrace_pointing_stars
alt: Two people on a rooftop terrace at night pointing at the same star, one with a short arm and one with a long stick, with the small angle between their arms highlighted.
scene: A flat rooftop terrace of an Indian apartment building at night, water tanks and a clothesline in the background, the city lights glowing below. Two people stand side by side looking up at a starry sky. On the left, a small boy of about 8 in shorts and a T-shirt points straight up with his short arm. On the right, his grandfather in his 70s in a shawl and spectacles points with a long bamboo stick, much longer than the boy's arm. Both are aiming at the same bright star, and a glowing dotted line extends from each arm to that star. Where their arms start, near their shoulders, a small arc is drawn between the two directions showing a tiny angle. Off to the side, a third person, the boy's mother in a nightie with a dupatta, points with a short arm at a completely different star far to the left, and a much wider arc shows a big angle between her arm and the boy's. A small inset in the corner shows two arrows of very different lengths pointing the same way, with the same small angle. Deep blue night light with a warm glow from the stairwell door, calm wondering mood. Labels: "SMALL ANGLE" by the narrow arc, "LENGTH IGNORED" by the inset, "DIFFERENT MEANING" by the wide arc.

key: A wedding invitation card printe
name: ch04_invitation_card_template
alt: A wedding-card printing shop using one card design and filling in each family's names, date and venue, keeping a record of which families received the old design.
scene: Inside a small wedding-card printing shop with walls covered in sample cards, glittering envelopes and ribbon spools. In the centre, an old letterpress machine with a fixed decorative frame plate: a border of paisleys, a simple floral motif, and blank lines in the middle. The printer, a moustached man in his 50s in a cotton shirt with ink-stained fingers, slides small metal letter blocks for names, a date and a venue into the blank lines of the frame, while the decorative border never changes. Beside him, three freshly printed cards dry on a rack, each with the same border but different names in the middle. On the counter, a young assistant in her 20s writes in a ledger, beside each family's name a small mark for which design version they got, and next to the counter lies a second, newer frame plate with a slightly different border, waiting to be used. A customer family, a father and a daughter, looks at the proof with smiles. Warm shop light with dust motes, busy festive mood. Labels: "TEMPLATE" on the fixed frame, "VARIABLES" on the metal name blocks, "VERSION" on the ledger.

key: A Mumbai local train map but dra
name: ch04_meaning_metro_map
alt: A metro map drawn by meaning, where idli, dosa and vada are neighbouring stations, laptop and keyboard sit on another line, and chai sits between food and morning.
scene: A large, colourful city metro map pinned on a station wall, with a few commuters looking at it, drawn so that stations are placed by meaning instead of geography. Each station is a small circle with an icon instead of a name. On a bright orange line, three neighbouring stations show an idli, a dosa and a vada, very close together. On a blue line further away, stations show a laptop, a keyboard and a mouse side by side. A green line holds a rising sun, an alarm clock and a newspaper. Exactly at an interchange between the orange food line and the green morning line sits a station with a steaming chai glass. One special station shows an apple and is drawn as an interchange touching both a fruit line, with a mango and a banana, and the technology line, with a phone. In the foreground, a young woman in a kurta with a backpack traces the orange line with her finger, while a small boy beside her points at the chai interchange and laughs. Station-platform light, curious mood. Labels: "SIMILAR = CLOSE" across the orange line, "TWO MEANINGS" by the apple station.

key: One-hot is like giving each of I
name: ch04_onehot_hash_profile
alt: Three ways to describe a person: a giant form with billions of tick boxes and one tick, grouping people by the last three digits of their phone number, and a short profile card.
scene: A triptych of three panels, each showing a way to describe the same young man, a cheerful fellow in his 20s in a striped T-shirt. LEFT panel: he stands in front of an absurdly huge paper form that stretches off into the distance like a road, covered with endless rows of tiny empty tick-boxes; a clerk on a tall ladder has ticked exactly one box near the top with a long pen, everything else blank. MIDDLE panel: a large wall of pigeonholes, each marked with three digits, where the young man has been dropped into one hole together with an elderly lady and a schoolgirl who look puzzled to be grouped with him, because their phone numbers end the same way. RIGHT panel: a neat small index card held in the young man's own hand, with a short list of small icons and bars like a mini profile, an age bar, a city pin, a speech bubble for language and a briefcase, and beside it a second card belonging to his colleague with almost the same bars, the two cards drawn close together. Bright neutral light, playful mood. Labels: "ONE-HOT" over the left panel, "HASHING" over the middle panel, "EMBEDDING" over the right panel.

key: CLIP is like a bilingual guide i
name: ch04_bilingual_guide_palace
alt: A tour guide matching a tourist's spoken description of a pink palace with many windows to the right photograph, while two separate one-language guides cannot compare.
scene: A sunny street in an old Rajasthani city with pink sandstone buildings, a camel cart passing in the background. In the centre, a lively tour guide in his 40s in a white kurta, a bright red turban and a moustache holds a fan of five postcards, picking out one that shows a tall pink palace facade with dozens of small latticed windows. In front of him, a foreign tourist in her 30s in a sun hat and a backpack speaks, her speech bubble showing a pink building and a cluster of tiny windows, and her face lights up as he holds up the matching postcard. A glowing thread links her speech bubble and the chosen postcard. On the left side of the picture, two other guides stand apart: one in a blue shirt holds only a notebook of written descriptions and speaks fluently, the other in a green shirt holds only a photo album, and the two look at each other with confused shrugs because they cannot compare words with pictures; a broken dotted line hangs between them. Bright desert sunlight with warm pink tones, cheerful mood. Labels: "CLIP" over the main guide, "TEXT ONLY" over the notebook guide, "IMAGE ONLY" over the album guide.

key: A post office sorter who has nev
name: ch04_post_sorter_closest_bag
alt: A post office sorter reading the address on an unfamiliar letter and dropping it into the bag whose label is closest in meaning, with two vaguely labelled bags confusing him.
scene: Inside a post office sorting room with dusty shelves and high windows, sacks hanging open on a wooden frame along the back wall. A postal sorter in his 50s in a khaki uniform, cap and spectacles holds up an envelope with a short handwritten address and a small coin-and-card sketch on it, reading it carefully.
