In front of him hang three canvas sacks, each with a large stencilled icon and no words: a rupee coin, a delivery van, and a phone with a small bug on it. A glowing dotted arc runs from the envelope to the payments sack, which is clearly the closest match, while fainter arcs reach the other two. Further to the right, a second, smaller scene shows two more sacks with nearly identical blank-looking labels and similar icons, and the same sorter stands before them flipping a coin in the air with a resigned face. A pile of unsorted letters waits in a wicker basket at his feet. Warm dusty sunlight through high windows, steady but slightly comic mood. Labels: "ZERO-SHOT" over the sorter, "CLOSEST LABEL" on the glowing arc, "TOO SIMILAR" over the coin-flip scene.

key: Finding the most similar-looking
name: ch04_stadium_steward_ann
alt: A visitor searching a 50,000-seat stadium for a face, with a steward guiding him to the right block and row instead of checking every seat.
scene: A huge cricket stadium seen from a high angle, the stands full of tiny faces in coloured shirts, divided into lettered blocks. In the lower left corner, a small exhausted man with a photo in his hand walks seat by seat along the first row, checking each face, with a long dotted path behind him and a sun setting, suggesting it would take all day. In the main part of the picture, the same man, now fresh, walks beside a helpful steward in his 30s in a bright reflective vest and cap, who points confidently up the stairs to one block, then one row. A sequence of three arrows shows the route: from the concourse to the block, from the block to the row, and from the row to a short group of a few dozen seats, where the man compares the photo with just those faces. Two blocks over, a faint glowing seat shows a face that matches even better, missed but close, with a small dotted outline. In a corner inset, workers repaint the block letters and rearrange signboards, hinting that the guide must be rebuilt when the crowd changes. Bright floodlights in early evening, energetic mood. Labels: "EXACT SEARCH" over the corner scene, "ANN INDEX" over the steward, "NEAR MISS" by the faint seat.

key: locker room: lockers spread acro
name: ch04_bank_locker_room
alt: A bank's locker system spread across branches, with duplicate keys at a second branch, CCTV and footfall counters, ID checks at the door, and a nightly ledger copy sent to the head office vault.
scene: A cut-away illustration of two bank branches and a head office linked by roads, drawn like a map with the roofs removed. In the first branch, rows of steel lockers line a vault room, half of them with numbers in one range; in the second branch across the road, the other half of the lockers continue the numbering. A messenger on a scooter carries a small sealed key pouch from the first branch to the second, where a duplicate key hangs on a board. At the entrance of the first branch, a security guard in a grey uniform checks a customer's photo ID card before letting her in, an elderly woman in a silk saree holding her locker key. On the ceiling, a CCTV camera and a small footfall counter with a digital number watch the vault. At the top right, the head office building has an underground vault where a clerk in a white shirt slides a thick ledger copy into a safe at night, a crescent moon visible above. Neutral daylight with a night-time corner, secure and orderly mood. Labels: "SHARDING" between the two branches, "REPLICATION" over the duplicate key, "BACKUP" over the head office vault.

key: A restaurant kitchen. Pre-retrie
name: ch04_kitchen_prep_fetch_plate
alt: A restaurant kitchen in three stations: prep where ingredients are washed, cut and labelled and the order is clarified, the store where the cook fetches ingredients, and plating where the best is arranged on top.
scene: A busy restaurant kitchen viewed from above, laid out as three stations from left to right connected by a steel counter. LEFT, prep: a young cook in her 20s with a hairnet washes and chops vegetables into labelled steel bowls, while a waiter beside her leans in with an order pad and a small question bubble showing an onion and a garlic bulb crossed out, checking a special dietary request. MIDDLE, fetch: a cook in his 30s with a white cap walks into a walk-in store room with labelled shelves and reaches for exactly the bowls and tins on his slip. RIGHT, plating: the head chef in her 40s in a black apron arranges a thali on a counter under a heat lamp, removing a stray chilli that doesn't belong into a waste bowl and placing the best pieces on top. In a small inset, a wrongly fetched ingredient looks exactly as glossy and appetising as the right one, with a tiny question mark, because in this case a wrong fetch is not obvious. Bright kitchen lights, steamy, coordinated mood. Labels: "PRE-RETRIEVAL" over the prep station, "RETRIEVAL" over the store room, "POST-RETRIEVAL" over the plating station.

key: Searching a long WhatsApp group
name: ch04_group_chat_small_to_big
alt: A person searching a long group chat for one short message about a refund, then scrolling up and down to read the surrounding messages before replying.
scene: A close, over-the-shoulder view of a young woman in her late 20s in a cotton kurta sitting on a sofa with a phone, a cup of tea on the armrest. The phone screen is drawn large beside her like a floating panel showing a long group chat with many message bubbles of different colours and little round avatars. At the top of the panel, a search bar holds a short query, and one short message bubble in the middle is highlighted with a glowing outline, reading "refund 30 days". Around that highlighted message, a soft window expands upward and downward to include two messages above and two below, drawn with a bracket and a magnifying lens, showing her reading the context. Higher up the chat, a few messages full of off-topic jokes and stickers sit outside the window, faded and grey, as if they might add noise if the window grew too big. Her thumb rests on the screen in mid-scroll, motion arrows above and below. Soft evening lamp light, focused and calm mood. Labels: "SMALL MATCH" on the highlighted message, "BIG CONTEXT" on the bracketed window, "NOISE" by the off-topic messages.

key: A reception desk at a government
name: ch04_govt_reception_router
alt: A receptionist at a government office routing a visitor to the right counter, rephrasing a vague request into a form name, imagining the finished form, and sending him to a city-specific desk.
scene: A busy government office hall with a row of numbered counters at the back, each with an icon above it: an ID card, a ration card with grain, and a computer monitor. In the foreground, a reception desk where a sharp, kind receptionist in her 40s in a cotton saree and spectacles listens to a confused visitor, a man in his 50s in a checked shirt holding a crumpled folder and saying something vague, his speech bubble showing a blurry card and a question mark. Above her head, three small thought bubbles show what she does: in the first, she rewrites his words into a neat little form with a title line; in the second, she pictures an imaginary completed form, ghostly and dotted, and uses it to search; in the third, she notices a city name on his folder and puts a small location pin on one specific counter. A large arrow from her desk points the man to the correct counter. A small clock beside her desk ticks with a coin under it, hinting each step costs time and money. Fluorescent office light, crowded but helpful mood. Labels: "ROUTER" over the receptionist, "REWRITE" over the first bubble, "HYDE" over the imagined form.

key: Asking two shopkeepers in a mark
name: ch04_two_shopkeepers_hybrid
alt: A shopper asking two shopkeepers at once: one who knows exact item codes and one who understands vague descriptions, with a dial setting how much to trust each.
scene: A narrow lane in a crowded wholesale market, with two small shops facing the viewer side by side. LEFT shop: a precise, thin shopkeeper in his 60s with spectacles and a pencil behind his ear runs his finger down a ledger of exact item codes and instantly pulls one specific packet of glucose biscuits of an exact weight from a shelf of identical-looking packets. RIGHT shop: a warm, chatty shopkeeper in her 40s in a bright saree listens to a description and confidently hands over a different packet of crunchy biscuits, with a small thought bubble showing a biscuit being dipped into a glass of tea. In the middle of the lane, a young customer in his 20s in a T-shirt holds a large brass dial with a pointer between the two shops, turning it towards the left for an exact request and towards the right for a vague one. Above, two little speech bubbles from the customer show an exact product code with a weight, and a biscuit with a teacup. Small scales on each shop's counter use different units, hinting the answers must be put on the same scale. Bright daylight with busy market colours, lively mood. Labels: "KEYWORD" over the left shop, "VECTOR" over the right shop, "ALPHA" on the dial.

key: central register (MongoDB wareho
name: ch04_stale_attendance_copy
alt: A class teacher calling names from a weekly-updated attendance copy, including students who left last Monday, while the central register in the office is already up to date.
scene: A primary-school classroom in the morning, with wooden benches, a blackboard and a ceiling fan, seen from the back of the room. At the front, a class teacher in her 40s in a cotton saree reads names aloud from a thin attendance copy, her speech bubble showing a child's face. Three of the names she calls belong to empty spaces on the benches, drawn as faint dotted outlines of children who are no longer there, and the other pupils turn around looking puzzled. Through an open door on the right, a small cut-away view shows the school office, where a clerk in a white shirt updates a thick central register with crossed-out rows for the children who left last Monday, a wall calendar beside him showing that day circled. Between the office and the classroom, a peon walks with a sync slip in his hand, and a large clock hangs over the corridor showing that he only makes this trip once a week. A small inset at the top shows the peon running back and forth many times, tired, suggesting that syncing more often costs effort. Bright morning light, mildly comic mood. Labels: "WAREHOUSE" over the central register, "FEATURE STORE" over the teacher's copy, "SYNC DELAY" over the clock.

key: A central kitchen for a restaura
name: ch04_central_kitchen_cold_store
alt: A restaurant chain's central kitchen: raw vegetables arrive at a warehouse, a prep kitchen cuts and portions them into labelled trays in a cold store, and both a training school and outlets take trays only from that cold store.
scene: A wide cut-away illustration of a restaurant chain's food hub, read left to right as a flow. LEFT: a warehouse loading bay where a truck unloads sacks of onions, crates of tomatoes and bunches of greens, a worker in a vest with a handcart. CENTRE: a bright prep kitchen where three cooks in white aprons and hairnets wash, cut and portion vegetables into identical steel trays, each tray with a small printed label; finished trays slide through a hatch into a large cold store with frosted shelves. RIGHT, two exits from the cold store only: on the upper side, a cooking school with a chef instructor and two trainee cooks taking trays to a practice counter; on the lower side, a delivery van carrying trays to a row of small restaurant outlets, where a cook at a hot stove adds spices and finishes the dish. A dotted arrow shows that neither the school nor the outlets go back to the warehouse directly. Cool white light in the cold store and warm light in the kitchens, efficient mood. Labels: "WAREHOUSE" over the loading bay, "FEATURE PIPELINE" over the prep kitchen, "FEATURE STORE" on the cold store door.

key: A dhobi (washerman) who collects
name: ch04_dhobi_weekly_batch
alt: A washerman who collects clothes all week and washes them together on Sunday, while a customer who needs a shirt on Wednesday finds it still unwashed.
scene: A riverside washing ghat and a neighbourhood lane shown in one composition. On the left, a weekly calendar strip runs across the top with days of the week, and below it a dhobi in his 40s in a vest and dhoti cycles from house to house on Monday through Saturday, the cloth bundle on his carrier growing larger each day. In the centre, on Sunday, the same dhobi and his wife stand knee-deep at a ghat with stone slabs, beating and rinsing a huge pile of clothes all at once, long lines of laundry drying in the sun behind them, very efficient. On the right, at a house door on Wednesday, a young man in a vest and towel holds up a printed invitation and looks dismayed, while his favourite blue shirt peeks out of the dhobi's still-unwashed bundle, because it won't be ready until Monday. A large circular arrow over the ghat shows the weekly cycle. A tiny clock beside the young man shows how long he must wait. Bright sunlight on the river, warm and slightly comic mood. Labels: "BATCH" over the Sunday washing, "STALE" by the unwashed shirt.

key: Batch is the BEST bus that comes
name: ch04_bus_vs_auto_streaming
alt: A city bus that comes every fifteen minutes on a fixed route for a daily commuter, versus an auto-rickshaw leaving the moment someone gets in for a hospital emergency.
scene: A busy city road scene split into two halves by a median with a small tree. LEFT: a red single-deck city bus at a bus stop with a timetable board showing a fifteen-minute clock symbol, office commuters in shirts and saris boarding calmly in a line with ticket passes, one man reading a newspaper while he waits. The bus is crowded but cheap and orderly. RIGHT: an auto-rickshaw pulling away instantly the moment a worried young man jumps in with his elderly father, who holds his chest, the driver already turning the handle, with motion lines and a small dust cloud; ahead along the road, a hospital building with a red cross is visible. A small inset at the top of the left half shows the same bus stop with buses arriving one after another every minute, the bus depot manager in the corner counting coins with a frown, hinting that running buses too often becomes expensive. Bright late-morning light, calm on the left and urgent on the right. Labels: "BATCH" over the bus, "STREAMING" over the auto-rickshaw, "EVERY MINUTE" on the inset.

key: Packing for a train trip: gather
name: ch04_packing_train_trip
alt: A family packing for a train trip: gathering things, discarding useless items, splitting into bags that fit the luggage rack, labelling each bag by contents, and tagging coach and seat.
scene: A living-room floor covered with luggage on the evening before a train journey, viewed from above. A family of four works around the room in a clockwise flow. Top left, the mother in a nightie with a dupatta gathers clothes, snacks, a water bottle and a shawl from cupboards into a big pile. Top right, the teenage son pulls out useless items, an old broken toy and an empty biscuit tin, and drops them into a dustbin. Bottom right, the father in a vest and lungi divides the pile into several bags, checking each bag against a cardboard outline of the train's luggage rack drawn on the floor to make sure it fits, one overstuffed bag being split in two. Bottom left, the young daughter writes small picture labels on each bag, a shirt, a snack, a toothbrush, and ties a luggage tag on each with a coach number and a seat number. In the centre, a printed train ticket lies on the floor. A small inset shows a bag on a weighing scale with a pointer, hinting that the real limit is measured, not guessed. Warm evening tube-light glow, busy family mood. Labels: "CLEAN" over the dustbin, "CHUNK" over the bags fitting the rack, "METADATA" on the luggage tags.

key: copy of the HR register in sync
name: ch04_branch_register_sync_four_ways
alt: Four ways a branch office keeps its copy of a head office register in sync: photocopying the whole register daily, asking for recently edited pages, a clerk writing every change in a diary, and reading the room's security camera log.
scene: A four-panel strip, two over two, each panel showing a branch-office clerk in her 30s in a sky-blue kurta trying to keep her copy of a thick register in sync with head office. Top left: at a photocopier, a peon feeds the entire register page by page, a huge stack of copies growing beside him, a calendar showing this happens daily. Top right: she phones head office and receives only a few pages marked with yesterday's date, but one page has been torn out of the register, leaving a ragged edge that nobody reports. Bottom left: at head office, every time an HR officer in a tie writes in the register, a second clerk beside him copies the same line into a small changes diary, looking tired, with a pile of finished diaries. Bottom right: in the register room, a CCTV camera on the ceiling records everything, and she sits at a monitor playing back the recorded footage, writing down each change, while the HR officer works undisturbed; small screens beside her show the footage in different formats. Office fluorescent light, methodical mood. Labels: "FULL SCAN" over the top-left panel, "TRIGGER" over the bottom-left panel, "LOG-BASED" over the bottom-right panel.

key: A railway reservation form that
name: ch04_reservation_form_strict_age
alt: A railway reservation clerk rejecting a form where the age is written in words and insisting on digits, while a train waits with correctly assigned berths.
scene: A railway reservation counter with a glass window and a speaking hole, a long queue behind. A stern but fair clerk in his 50s with a moustache and a pen behind his ear holds up a reservation form and taps one box with his finger, where the age has been written in words instead of digits, a red circle around it. The passenger, a young woman of about 23 in a kurta with a backpack, looks briefly annoyed but is already taking a pen to rewrite it as the number 23. On the counter, a small rubber stamp and a stack of accepted forms with neat digits. Through a window behind the clerk, a train waits on a platform with a printed reservation chart pasted on its coach door showing berths assigned correctly. In a small inset at the lower right, another form has a seat number box filled with a ridiculous big number that is still made of digits, and the clerk has stamped it anyway with a confused look, hinting that a type check is not a meaning check. Bright daylight through the window, brief friction but orderly mood. Labels: "STRICT CONFIG" over the clerk, "TYPE CHECK" over the circled box, "NOT MEANING" on the inset.

key: Ordering lunch from three restau
name: ch04_three_orders_parallel
alt: A man ordering lunch from three restaurants at once, waiting only for the slowest delivery while his phone sits idle, versus one cook trying to cook three dishes in one small kitchen.
scene: A split composition. MAIN LEFT PART: an office pantry where a relaxed young man in his late 20s in a polo shirt places three orders on his phone at the same time, then puts the phone face down on the table and sips water. Three dotted lines run out of the window to three different restaurants in the background, a biryani place, a dosa place and a chaat stall, and three delivery riders on scooters head back towards him. Each line has a small clock showing different times, and the longest clock is circled, showing he waits only for the slowest, not all three added up. A small sleeping zzz cloud floats above his idle phone. RIGHT PART, a smaller panel: a single cramped kitchen with one stove burner where one sweating cook in an apron tries to stir three pots at once by switching between them, making no faster progress, and a small inset beside it shows three separate kitchens each with its own cook working comfortably. key: parcels in, split into 2,373 pac

key: A translator at a bank counter:

Cool control-room light from screens, organised mood. Labels: "FACTORY" over the dispatcher, "STRATEGY" over the three vehicles, "NEW TYPE" over the bike bay.

key: Three tailors under one shop sig

On a rack near the door, finished garments from all three hang together, each with the same style of label attached at the collar. key: A kirana shop owner sorting rice
name: ch05_rice_sorting_pipeline
alt: A kirana owner preparing rice in stages: collecting sacks from several farms, removing repeated sacks, setting aside the inspector's sample sack, checking grain quality, looking for gaps, and ordering more.
scene: The back storeroom of a kirana shop, shown as a circular workflow around the room with arrows on the floor, viewed from above. Starting at the top left, a tempo unloads jute rice sacks from three different farms, each sack with a small painted farm symbol. Next, the owner, a sturdy man in his 50s in a vest and lungi with a pencil behind his ear, notices two sacks with the same lot number stencilled on them and pushes the duplicate aside. Next, his daughter, about 20, in a salwar kameez, pours a handful of grains onto a white plate and checks them under a lamp, picking out a broken grain and a small stone. Finally, the owner speaks on a phone placing an order, and an arrow loops back to the tempo at the start. Warm light from a high window, busy and careful mood. key: Training a new cook. An experien

In the foreground, a painter in his 40s in paint-splattered overalls and a cap stands at one wall with a roller. Beside that single wall, four items are lined up on a small stool: a paint swatch of the colour already on the wall, a sticky note with an arrow and a number showing how much to change it, and two small notebooks, one with a smooth curve of recent strokes and one with a jagged line of how bumpy they have been. Behind him, through doors and windows, dozens more walls each have the same set of four items beside them, piling up until a far room is filled to the ceiling with notebooks, as if a warehouse were needed. In a corner inset, a wall freshly painted in the wrong colour shows that the old colour is completely gone, a patch peeled to reveal nothing underneath, and the homeowner, a woman in her 30s, holds her head in dismay. Bright daylight with scaffolding shadows, busy but overwhelming mood. Labels: "WEIGHTS" over the swatch, "GRADIENT" over the sticky note, "OPTIMIZER STATES" over the two notebooks.

key: Moving house in a small car. LoR
name: ch05_moving_house_small_car
alt: A family moving house in a small car: full-size furniture plus a small box of new items, versus flat-packed furniture, folded leaflets and a roof carrier, fitting a much smaller car but needing unpacking at every stop.
scene: A split-panel scene on a residential street with a moving day in progress. LEFT panel: a bulky family car groaning under full-size wooden furniture, a sofa, a cupboard and a dining table tied on with ropes, plus one small cardboard box of new items on the back seat; the father, a man in his 40s in a T-shirt, pushes the boot door shut with effort. RIGHT panel: a much smaller hatchback where the same furniture has been flat-packed into thin boxes, about a quarter of the size, neatly stacked inside; the instruction leaflets have even been folded into tiny squares; a bag sits on a roof carrier where the overflow goes. The mother, in her 40s in a salwar kameez, ties the roof bag. In a small inset strip along the bottom of the right panel, the family stops at three places along the road and each time unpacks and assembles a chair before using it, a clock showing extra time. A final tiny detail shows an assembled flat-pack chair very slightly different from the original, with one knob in a different place. Bright morning light, busy and practical mood. Labels: "LORA" over the left panel, "QLORA" over the right panel, "PAGED" on the roof carrier.

key: Cooking biryani on a gas stove.
name: ch05_biryani_stove_hyperparams
alt: A cook making biryani on a gas stove where flame, turning the flame down, pot size, rounds, balanced salt, and a small counter each stand for a training setting.
scene: A home kitchen at dusk centred on a two-burner gas stove, a large handi of biryani on the main burner and a cook in her 50s in a cotton saree with sleeves tucked up. She turns the stove knob with one hand, and above the flame a curved gauge shows a burned black zone at the high end, a raw white zone at the low end and a green zone in the middle. A small timeline beside the stove shows the flame being lowered at the end for dum, with a lid sealed with dough. On the counter, measured portions of rice sit in pots of a fixed size, a little tick list on the wall counts the rounds of cooking for the whole order, and the spice box shows small even mounds so that no single spice dominates. The counter is small and nearly empty, with intermediate bowls being washed and put away rather than kept, and her teenage son stacks them in the drying rack. In a small inset, the cook tastes with a spoon, beside a little line chart that rises and settles, as if the model only tastes through such a curve. Warm golden kitchen light and rising steam, careful mood. Labels: "LEARNING RATE" on the flame gauge, "SCHEDULER" on the timeline, "BATCH SIZE" on the rice pots.

key: Parking a car in a tight spot. W
name: ch05_parking_lr_schedule
alt: A driver parking a car in a tight mall spot: gentle start, moderate speed to get close, creeping the last metre, with a crashed car and a car stuck far away as the too-high and too-low cases.
scene: A multi-level mall car park viewed from above, with painted lines and pillars. A small hatchback driven by a young woman in her late 20s, focused, leans forward over the wheel, and its path to a tight parking spot between two pillars is drawn as a curving dotted line with three coloured segments. At the start, near the entrance ramp, the path dots are close together with a tiny speedometer showing a gentle start. In the middle, the dots spread out showing a decent speed as the car approaches the spot. At the end, the dots crowd together again as she creeps the last metre, a parking attendant in a reflective vest guiding her with raised palms. In a small inset at the top left, another car has rammed into the back wall with a crumpled bumper and its driver looking embarrassed, the speedometer needle stuck at maximum. In a small inset at the top right, a third car is still near the entrance with its driver dozing, and a sign shows the mall closing time. Cool fluorescent car-park light, careful mood. Labels: "WARMUP" by the start segment, "DECAY" by the final segment, "TOO HIGH" on the crashed-car inset.

key: A teacher grading a class test t
name: ch05_teacher_tally_accumulation
alt: A teacher with a small desk reading eight answer sheets at a time, adding to a tally, and only adjusting her lesson plan after four rounds.
scene: A school staffroom with a small, cramped desk under a window, piled with stacks of answer sheets on the floor around it. A thoughtful teacher in her 40s in a printed cotton saree and spectacles reads a short stack of exactly eight answer sheets fanned out on the tiny desk, the most it can hold. Beside her, a notebook shows a running tally of marks with four groups of ticks, three already filled and the fourth being added. A small round counter on the desk shows the rounds, one to four. Behind her, a faded memory panel shows a younger version of her jumpily rewriting her lesson plan after every single answer sheet, crumpled lesson plans littering the floor. On the wall, her lesson plan board has only one pin moved, after the four rounds, a neat arrow showing a single adjustment. In the background, a big empty table in a different room sits with thirty-two sheets spread out on it, a place she cannot use. Soft afternoon light, calm and methodical mood. Labels: "MICRO-BATCH" over the eight sheets, "ACCUMULATE" over the tally, "ONE UPDATE" over the lesson plan board.

key: Revising for a board exam with o
name: ch05_revising_guidebook_overfit
alt: A student revising from one guidebook one, three and ten times, understanding it after three reads but memorising exact sentences after ten, with mock tests showing when to stop.
scene: A study room in a family flat, drawn as three moments of the same student, a boy of about 17 in a school T-shirt and shorts, each with a single thick guidebook. LEFT: after one read, he sits with the guidebook and a confused expression, bits of the book's diagrams floating loosely above his head with gaps between them. CENTRE: after three reads, he sits upright and confident, and the floating diagrams have joined together into a clear picture with arrows. RIGHT: after ten reads, he recites the book's exact sentences aloud with closed eyes, the words floating in a perfect copy of the book's typeface, but in front of him a real exam paper words a question differently and he stares at it, sweating. Along the bottom of the picture runs a line of small mock-test score cards after each read, rising, peaking at the third read with a flag stuck on it, and then dipping. His mother in the doorway holds the flagged card and taps it. Warm evening light, earnest mood. Labels: "UNDERFIT" over the left, "OVERFIT" over the right, "STOP HERE" on the flagged card.

key: A delivery rider choosing routes
name: ch05_rider_notebooks_adam
alt: A delivery rider keeping two notebooks for each road, average speed and bumpiness, driving fast on smooth roads and carefully on bumpy ones, with shorthand and phone-home variations.
scene: A city street map drawn from above with several roads of different textures, some smooth asphalt and some cratered with potholes. A delivery rider in his 20s in a red jacket and helmet rides a scooter with an insulated box on the back. Clipped to his handlebar are two small notebooks for the road he is on: one shows a smooth arrow and a speed number, the other shows a wiggly line for bumpiness. On a smooth road he leans forward and speeds up with motion lines; on a bumpy road shown further along, he slows down carefully. Three small insets in the corners show variations: one with the two notebooks written in tiny shorthand on a single small card; one where a whole neighbourhood shares a single summary sign instead of a notebook for every road; and one where the notebooks are left at home on a table and the rider stops to phone his mother who reads him an entry. A plain rider on another road follows only today's traffic, without any notebook. Bright midday light, busy and lively mood. Labels: "ADAM" over the rider with two notebooks, "8-BIT" over the shorthand card, "PAGED" over the phone-home inset.

key: A cricket selector who doesn
name: ch05_selector_trims_importance
alt: A cricket selector trimming each player's importance a little every match unless they earn it back, so the team wins through many contributors and copes when the star is out.
scene: A cricket team dressing room with lockers, kit bags and a whiteboard. A thoughtful selector in his 50s in a blazer and a team tie stands at the whiteboard where each player's name is replaced by a small figure with a vertical bar beside it showing his importance. The bars are all being trimmed by a small, equal sliver at the top with a pair of scissors the selector holds, and a few players with bat or ball in hand are adding back to their own bars by performing. The star batsman, a tall man with a sweatband, has a bar that was once enormous but is now more balanced with the others. Through the window behind, a match is underway on the ground where the star is sitting out injured with an ice pack while several teammates each score runs, a scoreboard showing the team still winning. In a small inset at the bottom corner, a different selector has trimmed so much that every bar is tiny and the players stand around confused. Bright daylight through the window, balanced mood. Labels: "WEIGHT DECAY" over the scissors, "MANY CONTRIBUTORS" over the match through the window.

key: Long-division homework on a smal
name: ch05_slate_gradient_checkpointing
alt: A student doing long division on a small slate, keeping only every second line and redoing missing lines when checking backwards.
scene: A close view of a child at a wooden school desk, a boy of about 10 in a school uniform with a chalk-dusted sleeve, working a long-division problem on a small black slate held in his lap. The slate is too small to hold every line of working, so only every second line is written in chalk, with blank gaps between them. A large floating copy of the slate beside him shows the gaps as dashed empty rows. In the next moment, checking his work backwards from the answer, he reaches a gap and quickly recomputes the missing line in a small speech bubble from the line just above, and an arrow shows the recomputed line filling the gap temporarily before being wiped again. On a much bigger slate hanging on the classroom wall behind him, a classmate has written every single line with no gaps, but that slate takes up the whole wall. A small clock on the desk shows that his way takes a little longer. In a tiny inset, each line on the slate turns into a heavy stacked block, hinting that redoing a line can be costly. Soft classroom daylight, focused mood. Labels: "CHECKPOINTS" on the kept lines, "RECOMPUTE" on the arrow, "LESS MEMORY" on the small slate.

key: Buying a used car to convert int
name: ch05_used_van_food_truck
alt: A man choosing a used van to convert into a food truck by checking its registration, budget and a test drive, then choosing between three workshops.
scene: A used-vehicle lot on the edge of a town, with a row of old vans, a small bus and a shed. In the foreground, an enthusiastic young man in his late 20s in a cap and a T-shirt holds a registration document up to the light, checking a stamped box for commercial use, while an older dealer in a vest and dhoti stands with keys. Beside him, a small van and a large bus are compared with little floating tags showing a fuel pump, a parking space and a price sticker, the van much cheaper on all three. In the middle distance, the same young man test-drives the van along a dusty local road with potholes and a speed breaker, the kind he will really use. On the far right, three workshops line the road: a large clean authorised service centre with a uniformed mechanic; a workshop where a mechanic follows a printed job card clipped to the wall; and a small speedy garage with a single bay and a racing-style mechanic working very fast. The young man looks between them with a thinking face. Bright afternoon light, hopeful mood. Labels: "LICENSE" on the registration document, "BUDGET" over the price tags, "JOB CARD" on the printed card in the second workshop.

key: Training a new RJ (radio jockey)
name: ch05_rj_trainee_clips
alt: A trainee radio jockey learning to sound like a famous host from a small box of the host's clips plus a larger box of general radio clips, each ending with the station jingle, with a few clips set aside for testing.
scene: A small radio studio with soundproof foam on the walls, a microphone on an arm, a mixing desk and a glowing red on-air lamp. A trainee radio jockey in his early 20s in a hoodie with headphones sits at the desk listening intently, mouthing words, a notebook open. On the shelf in front of him are two boxes of recorded clips shown as small cassettes: a small box with the famous host's portrait sketch on it, holding only a modest number of clips, and a much bigger box of assorted general radio clips. A producer in her 30s in a denim jacket feeds clips from both boxes into a player, and at the end of every clip a tiny musical note icon pops out of the speaker, the station jingle, marking the end of a segment. On a separate side table, a little group of clips sits in a tray with a stop sign, set aside to test the trainee later. A thought bubble above the trainee shows two faces blending, the host's and a generic announcer's, hinting his voice may get diluted. Warm studio lighting, focused mood. Labels: "STYLE DATA" on the small box, "GENERAL DATA" on the big box, "EOS" by the jingle note.

key: A car dashboard on a long drive.
name: ch05_car_dashboard_loss_curves
alt: A driver on a highway watching a car dashboard: a fuel-efficiency readout, a GPS arrival estimate getting worse, and a calm RPM needle with a rev limiter.
scene: The inside of a car on a long highway drive, viewed from the back seat over the driver's shoulder, the road stretching ahead through fields and distant hills. The driver, a woman in her 30s in sunglasses and a cotton shirt, glances at the dashboard, which is drawn large and clear. On the left of the dashboard, a fuel-efficiency readout shows a line that has improved and settled. On the right, a GPS screen shows an arrival-time estimate whose small trend line has started to rise again, a tiny red arrow pointing up, while the fuel line keeps looking great, and her eyebrows knit in concern. In the centre, a large RPM gauge with a calm needle in a safe zone, and at the top of the gauge, a red band with a small limiter icon that stops the needle from crossing it. In a small inset, the same dashboard on a different trip shows the needle pinned in the red, smoke rising from the bonnet. A passenger in the back seat holds a map and points at the true destination. Bright highway sunlight, alert mood. Labels: "TRAINING LOSS" on the fuel readout, "VALIDATION LOSS" on the GPS screen, "CLIPPING" on the limiter.

key: Teaching a child manners with on
name: ch06_child_manners_say_not_that
alt: A mother teaching a child table manners at dinner, holding up a card with the polite request beside a crossed-out card with the rude one.
scene: A family dinner table in a modest Indian home in the evening, with steel plates, a bowl of dal, rotis in a cloth and a small glass salt shaker at the far end. A little boy of about 6 in a striped T-shirt reaches across the table, while his mother, a warm woman in her 30s in a cotton salwar kameez, kneels beside his chair holding up two picture cards. The card in her right hand has a smiling face, a pair of folded hands and an arrow towards the salt shaker, with a big green tick. The card in her left hand shows a grumpy face and a grabbing hand towards the same shaker, with a big red cross. The boy looks from one card to the other, and a speech bubble above him shows the folded hands and the salt shaker, choosing the polite version. On the other side of the table, the grandfather in a white kurta smiles, and an older sister of about 12 quietly passes the salt. In a small inset at the top, an earlier lesson shows the mother holding only the green card, and the boy forgets it soon after. Warm tube-light glow, gentle family mood. Labels: "CHOSEN" on the green-tick card, "REJECTED" on the red-cross card.

key: seasoning takes a handful of tas
name: ch06_seasoning_vs_culinary_school
alt: Split scene: a good cook adjusting the seasoning of one dish after a few tastings, versus a beginner spending years at a culinary school learning the whole cuisine, with a machine producing tasting pairs in bulk.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: in a home kitchen, a skilled cook in her 40s in a saree with an apron tastes a spoonful of rasam, while her husband holds two small bowls and points at one of them; a tiny counter on the wall shows only a handful of tasting rounds, and she adds a pinch of salt with a satisfied look. RIGHT panel: a huge culinary institute with many floors and classrooms, where a beginner in a white chef's coat, about 19, moves through classes on tandoor, South Indian, sweets and street food, a calendar beside him showing years flipping by and stacks of textbooks. At the bottom of the right panel, a small conveyor machine at the institute prints out pairs of small tasting bowls endlessly into crates, thousands of pairs stacked high, showing why large providers can collect millions of pairs. The two halves are lit differently: soft kitchen light on the left and bright institutional light on the right. Labels: "TASK-SPECIFIC" over the left panel, "PROVIDER-SCALE" over the right panel, "BULK PAIRS" on the machine.

key: Writing exam answers versus mark
name: ch06_writing_vs_marking
alt: A teacher marking a big stack of answer sheets quickly while a student struggles to write a single model answer, with all the sheets looking alike because they came from the same guidebook.
scene: A school staffroom split by a wooden partition, with a big wall clock above showing the same time on both sides. LEFT: a student of about 16 in a white uniform sits at a desk with a crumpled sheet and a pencil, slowly writing one model answer, his forehead creased, eraser crumbs everywhere, and only the first few lines done. RIGHT: a calm teacher in her 50s in a cotton saree with spectacles on a chain moves through a tall stack of fifty answer sheets, ticking and ranking them quickly with a red pen, a neat finished pile growing beside her. A small banner over her desk shows sheets being placed in order from best to worst with numbers. In a small inset at the bottom right, the teacher fans out several sheets and they all have the same handwriting style and the same diagram copied from one guidebook, which sits on a shelf behind her, and she raises an eyebrow because there are no surprising answers in the pile. Bright morning light through tall windows, contrasting slow effort with quick judgement. Labels: "WRITING IS SLOW" over the student, "RANKING IS FAST" over the teacher, "SAME GUIDE" on the inset.

key: Asking one aunty for a biryani r
name: ch06_aunties_biryani_styles
alt: A young cook collecting biryani recipes from three aunties from different cities, each improvising a little, with one over-improvised biryani containing chocolate.
scene: A lively family kitchen during a festival, with a long counter, three large handis and a crowd of relatives. A young man in his 20s in a kurta, holding a notebook and a pen, stands in the centre writing down recipes. Around him three aunties each cook their own biryani in a different style. The first, from Hyderabad, a woman in her 50s in a silk saree, layers rice and meat in a sealed handi with dough around the lid. The second, from Lucknow, a woman in her 60s in a chikan kurta, gently ladles fragrant yakhni stock over rice. The third, from Kolkata, a woman in her 40s in a cotton saree with a red bindi, adds a whole boiled potato and an egg. Each aunty has a small dial above her head, showing how much she improvises, set low to middle. A fourth, younger cousin at the end of the counter has his dial turned to the maximum and is dropping a chocolate bar into his handi, with the family making shocked faces. Grandmother in the background tastes the three proper biryanis and nods at one. Warm festive light and steam, cheerful mood. Labels: "DIVERSE SOURCES" over the three aunties, "TEMPERATURE" on the dials, "TOO HIGH" over the cousin.

key: A clipping service that cuts quo
name: ch06_clipping_service_rules
alt: A clipping service worker cutting quotes from newspapers by strict rules: whole sentences only, starting with a capital and ending with a full stop, with too-short pieces thrown away.
scene: A small clipping-service office with stacks of newspapers, a long table and a bin underneath it. A meticulous worker in his 50s in a sweater vest and thick spectacles cuts out quotes from newspaper columns with sharp scissors along precise sentence boundaries. On the wall behind him hangs a printed rule poster with three simple pictograms: a pair of scissors cutting at a full stop, a large capital letter at the start with a tick, and a short ruler showing a minimum length. On the table, accepted clippings are pinned in a neat row, each starting with a big capital and ending in a dot. Next to the bin, discarded scraps show a clipping that ends in three dots, one that starts in the middle of a word, and a tiny fragment shorter than a line, all with small red crosses. In a small inset at the bottom right, one accepted clipping follows all the rules perfectly but has a yawning face drawn next to it, hinting that it is dull and useless anyway. Soft office light with dust in the air, precise mood. Labels: "FILTERS" over the rule poster, "FORM NOT MEANING" on the inset.

key: Out of 2,970 mangoes picked, abo
name: ch06_mango_grader_export_box
alt: A mango grader at an orchard checking size and colour, sending about half the mangoes to an export box, while their taste is never checked.
scene: An orchard packing shed in summer, open on one side to rows of mango trees heavy with fruit. A large heap of freshly picked mangoes lies on a jute mat on the left. In the centre, a grader in his 40s in a vest and a cotton towel on his head sits on a low stool beside a wooden sorting frame with a round hole of a fixed size and a colour chart card nailed beside it showing golden-yellow shades. He holds up one mango to the hole and the colour chart, and sorts quickly: mangoes that pass go to the right into a neat cardboard export box lined with straw; those that fail go to the left into a basket for the local market. About half the heap is in each. On the right, an export agent in a crisp shirt and cap tapes the export box shut. In a small inset at the bottom, a woman bites into a perfect-looking mango from the export box and makes a sour face, while a lumpy mango from the local basket is shown with a sweet smiling sparkle, because the grader never tasted them. Bright summer sunlight filtering through the shed roof, busy harvest mood. Labels: "FILTER" over the sorting frame, "PASS" on the export box, "NOT TASTED" on the inset.

key: have the owner taste every dish,
name: ch06_head_taster_kl_rule
alt: A restaurant owner training a head taster, who then scores the cooks' experiments, while a rule card keeps recipes close to the house original so cooks do not drown dishes in butter.
scene: A restaurant kitchen shown in two connected parts. In a small inset at the top left, the owner, a man in his 60s with a grey beard in a white kurta, sits with a younger head taster in a chef's jacket, both tasting two bowls side by side and the taster noting the owner's choice in a notebook, a calendar showing one week. The main scene: the busy kitchen where three cooks experiment with dishes on a long counter, and the head taster, now alone, walks along tasting each one and holding up a numbered score card. Pinned above the counter is a framed house recipe card with a short elastic band drawn from it to each cook's pot, showing they can stray only a little from the original. At the far end, one cook in a bandana has ignored the band and is pouring a whole slab of butter into his pot, and the taster has given it a high score, while the original recipe card glows red in warning. A small window in the back shows the owner peeking in only occasionally. Warm kitchen light, lively but watchful mood. Labels: "REWARD MODEL" over the head taster, "KL PENALTY" on the elastic bands, "REWARD HACKING" over the butter cook.

key: A tailor altering a suit with re
name: ch06_tailor_removable_sleeves
alt: A tailor comparing a suit before and after alteration by simply detaching new removable sleeves, with no second suit needed, contrasted with a fully altered suit that needs the original kept separately.
scene: A small tailoring shop with bolts of cloth on shelves, a large mirror and a dress form on a stand. In the centre, an experienced tailor in his 60s with a measuring tape around his neck and a pincushion on his wrist holds up a dark suit jacket on the dress form whose sleeves attach with neat buttons and hidden loops at the shoulder. He has just unbuttoned one new sleeve with a different finish and holds it in his other hand, revealing the original shoulder and jacket underneath, unchanged. A customer in his 30s in a shirt and tie watches in the mirror and smiles, able to compare before and after with one jacket. The other new sleeve is still attached. On the right side of the shop, a second rack shows a different situation: a suit that has been fully re-stitched all over with chalk marks everywhere, and next to it a second, original suit hanging in a garment bag kept just for comparison, taking up extra space. Warm afternoon light through the shop window, crafty and clever mood. Labels: "ADAPTER" on the detachable sleeve, "BASE MODEL" on the jacket body, "FULL FINE-TUNE" over the right-side rack.

key: A cricket coach tracking a batte
name: ch06_coach_tracking_nets_metrics
alt: A cricket coach in the nets tracking good shots rising, edges falling, the gap growing then levelling, and the share of middled balls rising but never reaching all of them.
scene: A cricket net session in the late afternoon, a young batter in whites and a helmet playing shots against a bowler while a coach watches from just outside the net. The coach, a woman in her 40s in a team tracksuit with a cap and a whistle, holds a clipboard on which the picture shows a small hand-drawn chart: a line for good shots rising, a line for edges falling, and the shaded space between them widening and then flattening. Beside it, a tally of middled balls shows most balls ticked but a few still crossed. The batter cracks a clean cover drive with a ringing sound mark, and a fielder chases. In a small inset at the top right, a different session shows the bowler as a small child lobbing slow balls and the batter middling every single one in the first over, with the coach shaking her head, because the bowling is too easy. Another small inset at the bottom right shows the coach also watching the batter's footwork closely, noticing his stance has become odd even though the numbers look good. Golden late-afternoon light, focused and encouraging mood. Labels: "REWARDS" on the two lines, "MARGIN" on the shaded gap, "TOO EASY" on the top inset.
